nodes.name: Machine learning (vs. classical programming)
nodes.definition: A programming paradigm in which a system is given data and the expected answers and learns the rules that map one to the other, instead of a human writing the rules.
nodes.chapter: Deep Learning with Python, Third Edition
aliases: Machine learning (as a subfield of AI)

nodes.name: Overfitting
nodes.definition: The state where a model fits the training data so closely, including its noise and quirks, that its performance on new data degrades.
nodes.chapter: Deep Learning with Python, Third Edition
aliases: Overfitting (as seen in a validation curve)

nodes.name: Deep learning
nodes.definition: A subfield of machine learning that learns successive layers of increasingly meaningful representations from data.
aliases: Deep learning (as a subfield of machine learning)

nodes.name: Learning representations from data
nodes.definition: Automatically finding transformations of input data that make a task (e.g., classification) easier.

nodes.name: Democratization of AI
nodes.definition: The authors' goal of putting understanding of deep learning — how it works, where it fails, and how to apply it — into the hands of as many people as possible, including non-researchers.

nodes.name: Standard (universal) machine learning workflow
nodes.definition: A repeatable process for approaching and solving machine learning problems, which the book promises you will know by the end.

nodes.name: Literate programming
nodes.definition: Writing a program as an explanation for human readers, with executable code embedded in prose; the book calls itself 'simultaneously a prose explanation of deep learning concepts and a runnable Python program'.

nodes.name: Keras backend
nodes.definition: The low-level deep learning framework (TensorFlow, PyTorch or JAX) on which Keras code runs.

nodes.name: AI hype vs. real progress
nodes.definition: The gap between media and marketing claims about AI and what the technology can demonstrably do; the authors ask practitioners to be able to tell the two apart.

nodes.name: Artificial intelligence (AI)
nodes.definition: The effort to automate intellectual tasks normally performed by humans (book's definition on this page).

nodes.name: Symbolic AI (handcrafted rules)
nodes.definition: The approach of achieving intelligence by having programmers handcraft a sufficiently large set of explicit rules for manipulating knowledge; named 'symbolic AI' on p.27.

nodes.name: Classical programming (rules written by a human)
nodes.definition: The usual way to make a computer do useful work: a human programmer writes down rules — a program — to be followed to turn input data into appropriate answers.
aliases: Classical programming (rules written by a human)

nodes.name: Lady Lovelace's objection
nodes.definition: Lovelace's 1843 claim that the Analytical Engine 'has no pretensions whatever to originate anything' and can only do what we know how to order it to perform; named and discussed by Turing in 1950.

nodes.name: Turing test
nodes.definition: A thought experiment introduced in Turing's 1950 paper 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence'; per footnote 2, a conceptual device for a philosophical discussion about cognition, not a literal benchmark the field should aim to pass.

nodes.name: Training
nodes.definition: The process by which a machine learning system, presented with many examples relevant to a task, finds statistical structure in them and arrives at rules for automating the task.

nodes.name: Measure of success (precursor of the loss function)
nodes.definition: The third ingredient of machine learning: a way to measure whether the algorithm is doing a good job, i.e. the distance between its current output and the expected output.
aliases: Measure of success (precursor of the loss function)

nodes.name: Machine learning as an engineering discipline
nodes.definition: The authors' characterization: machine learning is related to statistics but not reducible to it, deals with large complex datasets where classical statistical analysis is impractical, has comparatively little mathematical theory, and is a hands-on field driven by empirical findings and by software and hardware advances.
aliases: Machine learning as an engineering discipline

nodes.name: Learning (as feedback-driven adjustment)
nodes.definition: The adjustment step in which a measurement of the distance between the algorithm's current output and the expected output is used as a feedback signal to change the way the algorithm works.

nodes.name: Representation
nodes.definition: A different way to look at, represent or encode data; machine learning models are about finding representations of their input that make the data more amenable to the task at hand.

nodes.name: Coordinate change as a transformation
nodes.definition: Re-expressing data points relative to a new set of axes; in figure 1.4 this transformation turns an inseparable-looking point cloud into one where black and white points lie on opposite sides of an axis.

nodes.name: Feedback signal
nodes.definition: The measurement of the distance between the algorithm's current output and its expected output, used to adjust the algorithm.

nodes.name: Hypothesis space
nodes.definition: The predefined set of operations (data transformations) that a machine learning algorithm searches through.

nodes.name: Hand-designed representations (feature engineering)
nodes.definition: Designing data transformations by hand using human understanding of the problem — e.g. counting closed loops or computing pixel histograms for digits.

nodes.name: Depth of a model
nodes.definition: The number of layers that contribute to a model of the data.

nodes.name: Shallow learning
nodes.definition: Machine learning approaches that learn only one or two layers of representations of the data.

nodes.name: Neural network
nodes.definition: The kind of model used in deep learning: literal layers stacked on top of each other, which learn layered representations.

nodes.name: Information distillation
nodes.definition: The authors' mental model of a deep network: a multistage process in which information passes through successive filters and comes out increasingly purified, i.e. useful for the task.

nodes.name: Weights (parameters) of a layer
nodes.definition: The numbers stored in a layer that specify the transformation it applies to its input; the layer's transformation is parameterized by its weights.

nodes.name: Optimizer
nodes.definition: The component that uses the loss score as a feedback signal to adjust the weights a little, in a direction that lowers the loss for the current example; it implements the Backpropagation algorithm.

nodes.name: Backpropagation
nodes.definition: The central algorithm in deep learning, implemented by the optimizer, that determines how to adjust the weights so as to lower the loss; explained in detail in chapter 2.

nodes.name: Training loop
nodes.definition: The repeated process in which the network processes an example, the loss is computed, and the weights are adjusted a little in the correct direction, so that the loss score decreases.
aliases: Training loop and the trained network

nodes.name: End-to-end deep learning model
nodes.definition: A single, simple model that replaces a sophisticated multistage pipeline by learning all features in one pass from raw input to output.

nodes.name: Scalability of deep learning
nodes.definition: Deep learning is highly amenable to parallelization on GPUs or specialized hardware and so takes full advantage of Moore's law; training on small batches allows datasets of arbitrary size (p.35).

nodes.name: Foundation model
nodes.definition: A large model trained on humongous amounts of data that can be used across many new tasks with little retraining, or even none at all.

nodes.name: Self-supervised learning
nodes.definition: Learning in which the targets of Figure 1.8 are taken from the input itself — the model learns to reconstruct its input (a sharp image from a noisy one, the next word in a sentence).

nodes.name: Prompting
nodes.definition: Solving a new problem by querying the knowledge representations a foundation model has learned and returning the output most likely to be associated with the prompt.

nodes.name: Generative AI
nodes.definition: Deep learning applications — chatbot assistants, image generation services — that produce informative or creative content in response to simple prompts.

nodes.name: Versatility and reusability
nodes.definition: Deep learning models can be trained on additional data without restarting from scratch (continuous online learning) and are repurposable for new tasks.

nodes.name: The three waves of the deep learning revolution
nodes.definition: The authors' periodization of the past decade: remarkable results on perceptual tasks (2013–2017), fast progress on natural language processing (2017–2022), and transformative generative AI applications (2022 to now).
aliases: The three waves of the deep learning revolution

nodes.name: Deep learning breakthroughs
nodes.definition: Major successes on long-standing hard problems: chatbots, programming assistants, photorealistic image generation, human-level image classification, speech and text transcription, improved translation and text-to-speech, public autonomous driving, better recommender systems, superhuman game play.

nodes.name: Cognitive automation
nodes.definition: The encoding and operationalization of human skills and knowledge in a computer system — the authors' more accurate name for what today's 'artificial intelligence' does.

nodes.name: Intelligence as adaptability (cognitive autonomy)
nodes.definition: The ability to face the unknown, adapt to it, and learn from it; contrasted with automation, which can only handle situations it was trained on or programmed for.

nodes.name: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) hype
nodes.definition: The claim that human-level general intelligence — or a superintelligence beyond humans — is about to arrive.

nodes.name: Short-term hype
nodes.definition: Inflated near-term expectations about a technology, here AI, that outrun its actual delivered impact.

nodes.name: AI winter
nodes.definition: A period of disappointment, skepticism and scarce funding that follows a phase of intense optimism about AI when the technology falls short of inflated expectations.

nodes.name: The 2023–2025 AI bubble
nodes.definition: The author's characterization of a period in which AI investment (over $200B/yr, mainly data centers and GPUs) far exceeds AI revenue (around $30B/yr), sustained by expectations of future capabilities.

nodes.name: Expert systems
nodes.definition: 1980s systems, a new take on symbolic AI, that encoded expert knowledge as explicit rules; adopted by large companies that built in-house AI departments.

nodes.name: Long-term vision vs. short-term hype
nodes.definition: The authors' guiding distinction: near-term claims (imminent AGI, 100× productivity, the current investment bubble) deserve skepticism, while the long-term expectation that AI will be applied to nearly every process in society deserves belief.

nodes.name: The internet analogy for AI adoption
nodes.definition: The comparison, used twice on the page, between AI now and the internet in 1995 (hard to see its relevance before deployment) and in 1998–2003 (overhyped, crashed, then transformed everything).
aliases: The internet analogy for AI adoption

nodes.name: AI as an accelerator of science
nodes.definition: The use of AI to assist human scientists in making discoveries, which the 2017 text called the most important of AI's future roles.
aliases: AI as an accelerator of science

nodes.name: MNIST dataset
nodes.definition: A classic dataset of grayscale handwritten-digit images, 28 × 28 pixels, labeled 0–9: 60,000 training images and 10,000 test images, assembled by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in the 1980s.

nodes.name: Class, sample, label

nodes.name: Layer
nodes.definition: The core building block of a neural network: a data-processing module that takes data in and returns it transformed into a (hopefully) more useful representation.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Dense (fully connected) layer
nodes.definition: A layer in which every output unit is connected to every input value by a learned weight, plus a bias, followed by an activation function.

nodes.name: Sequential model
nodes.definition: A Keras model that is a plain stack of layers, each feeding the next, mapping a single input to a single output.

nodes.name: Softmax classification layer
nodes.definition: A final layer with as many units as classes and a softmax activation, so its output is a probability distribution over the classes.

nodes.name: Metrics
nodes.definition: Quantities monitored during training and testing to judge the model; here, accuracy, the fraction of correctly classified images.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Preprocessing (reshape and rescale)
nodes.definition: Transforming raw input data into the shape, dtype and value range the model expects before training.

nodes.name: Sparse categorical cross-entropy loss
nodes.definition: The loss used for multiclass classification with integer labels; it measures how far the predicted probability distribution is from the true class.

nodes.name: Epoch and batch size
nodes.definition: An epoch is one full pass over the training data; the batch size is the number of samples processed per weight update.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: fit()
nodes.definition: The Keras method that trains a compiled model on training data and targets.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: predict() and reading softmax outputs

nodes.name: evaluate()
nodes.definition: The Keras method that computes a model's loss and metrics over a dataset of inputs and targets.

nodes.name: argmax decision rule
nodes.definition: Choosing the class with the largest predicted probability.

nodes.name: Rank and axes

nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Scalar (rank-0 tensor)
nodes.definition: A tensor that contains only one number; also called scalar tensor, rank-0 tensor or 0D tensor.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Vector (rank-1 tensor)
nodes.definition: An array of numbers; a tensor with exactly one axis.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Matrix (rank-2 tensor)
nodes.definition: An array of vectors; a tensor with two axes, rows and columns, picturable as a rectangular grid of numbers.

nodes.name: Shape
nodes.definition: A tuple of integers describing how many dimensions a tensor has along each axis.

nodes.name: Data type (dtype)
nodes.definition: The type of the data contained in a tensor, such as float16, float32, float64, uint8 or bool (and string in TensorFlow).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Rank-3 and higher-rank tensors
nodes.definition: Tensors obtained by packing matrices (rank 3, a cube of numbers), then packing rank-3 tensors (rank 4), and so on.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Indexing the first axis to get one sample
nodes.definition: Selecting `train_images[i]` returns the i-th sample, a (28, 28) matrix, because the first axis of a data tensor enumerates samples.

nodes.name: Grayscale image as a matrix
nodes.definition: A grayscale image is a matrix of pixel intensities; MNIST stores each digit as a 28 x 28 uint8 matrix with values 0-255.

nodes.name: Tensor slicing
nodes.definition: Selecting a sub-tensor by specifying an index or an index range (`start:stop`) along each axis of a tensor.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Data batch
nodes.definition: A group of samples of fixed size (the batch size) that a model processes together in one step, obtained by slicing the samples axis.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Standard data tensor shapes
nodes.definition: The four templates covering almost all data: vector `(samples, features)` rank 2; timeseries `(samples, timesteps, features)` rank 3; images `(samples, height, width, channels)` rank 4; video `(samples, frames, height, width, channels)` rank 5.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Vector data
nodes.definition: A dataset in which each data point is a vector of numerical attributes, stored as a rank-2 tensor `(samples, features)`.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Timeseries / sequence data tensor
nodes.definition: A rank-3 tensor `(samples, timesteps, features)` in which each sample is a sequence of feature vectors; the time axis is axis 1 by convention.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: One-hot (binary) encoding
nodes.definition: Representing a categorical symbol from an alphabet of size K as a length-K vector that is all zeros except for a 1 at the symbol's index.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks
aliases: One-hot encoding as an identity-matrix lookup

nodes.name: Video data tensor
nodes.definition: A rank-5 tensor `(samples, frames, height, width, color_depth)`: a batch of videos, each a sequence of color-image frames.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Tensor operation
nodes.definition: A function applied to numeric tensors that returns a tensor (addition, product, relu, …); the book's claim is that all transformations learned by deep networks reduce to a handful of these.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: relu (REctified Linear Unit)
nodes.definition: The element-wise function relu(x) = max(x, 0): positive entries pass through, negative entries become 0.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Element-wise operation
nodes.definition: An operation applied independently to each entry of the tensor(s) involved, such as relu, addition, subtraction or multiplication of same-shaped tensors.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Vectorized implementation
nodes.definition: An implementation that processes many tensor entries in parallel (or in one compiled loop) instead of one entry per interpreted step; the term comes from the vector-processor supercomputers of 1970-1990.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: BLAS (Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms)
nodes.definition: A standard set of low-level, highly parallel, efficient tensor-manipulation routines, typically implemented in Fortran or C, to which NumPy delegates the heavy lifting of its built-in operations.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Broadcasting
nodes.definition: The rule by which, when possible and unambiguous, the smaller tensor in an element-wise operation is expanded to match the shape of the larger tensor.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Element-wise operation
nodes.definition: An operation applied independently to each entry of a tensor (or to each pair of corresponding entries of two same-shape tensors).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Tensor product (dot product, matmul)
nodes.definition: The operation that multiplies two tensors by summing products along a shared axis. For two vectors of the same length it is the sum of element-wise products, a scalar.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Matrix product (matmul of two matrices)
nodes.definition: For x of shape (m, n) and y of shape (n, p), matmul(x, y) is the (m, p) matrix whose entry (i, j) is the vector product of row i of x and column j of y. Defined iff x.shape[1] == y.shape[0].
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Matrix–vector product
nodes.definition: For x of shape (m, n) and y of shape (n,), matmul(x, y) is the vector of length m whose i-th coefficient is the vector product of row i of x with y.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Higher-rank tensor product rule
nodes.definition: The product of tensors of any rank follows the 2-D compatibility rule: the last axis of the first operand must equal the first axis of the second; it is contracted and the remaining axes are concatenated.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Tensor reshaping
nodes.definition: A tensor operation that rearranges a tensor's coefficients into a target shape with the same total number of elements.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Transposition
nodes.definition: Exchanging the rows and columns of a matrix so that x[i, :] becomes x[:, i]; the shape (m, n) becomes (n, m).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Geometric interpretation of tensor operations
nodes.definition: Reading a tensor's contents as the coordinates of points in a geometric space, so that every tensor operation becomes a geometric transformation.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Vector addition as chaining arrows
nodes.definition: The sum of two vectors is found by placing the second arrow's tail at the first arrow's head; the sum runs from the origin to the final head.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Translation (vector addition)
nodes.definition: Moving every point of an object by the same vector, so the object is copied to a new location without distortion.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Rotation matrix
nodes.definition: The 2 × 2 matrix `[[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]]` whose product with a 2-D vector rotates it counterclockwise by θ about the origin.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Scaling (diagonal) matrix
nodes.definition: A diagonal 2 × 2 matrix `[[s_x, 0], [0, s_y]]`; multiplying by it scales the x coordinate by s_x and the y coordinate by s_y.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Linear transform
nodes.definition: A map implemented by a product with an arbitrary matrix: x ↦ W @ x.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Affine transform
nodes.definition: A linear transform (matrix product) combined with a translation (vector addition): y = W @ x + b.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Composition of affine transforms
nodes.definition: Applying one affine transform after another yields a single affine transform: W2 @ (W1 @ x + b1) + b2 = (W2 @ W1) @ x + (W2 @ b1 + b2).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Activation function (why it is necessary)
nodes.definition: A nonlinear function, applied element-wise after a layer's affine computation, that prevents stacked Dense layers from collapsing into a single affine map.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Deep learning as geometric transformation
nodes.definition: A neural network is a chain of simple geometric transformations (tensor operations) that together implement a very complex geometric transformation of the input data in a high-dimensional space.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: The crumpled-paper image
nodes.definition: Two sheets of coloured paper (two classes) crumpled together into a ball (the input data); the network must find a transformation that uncrumples them so the classes are cleanly separable.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Manifold (data manifold)
nodes.definition: A continuous surface, like the crumpled sheet of paper, on which the data of a class lies inside a high-dimensional space.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Random initialization
nodes.definition: Filling the weight matrices with small random values before training.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Forward pass
nodes.definition: Running the model on a batch of inputs x to obtain predictions y_pred.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Gradient descent
nodes.definition: The optimization technique that uses the gradient of the loss with respect to the model's coefficients to move all coefficients at once in a direction that decreases the loss.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks
aliases: Gradient descent as a 'stupid' search process

nodes.name: Differentiability
nodes.definition: The property of a function that transforms its input in a smooth and continuous way, so that a small change of the input produces a small change of the output whose direction can be inferred.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Gradient
nodes.definition: A mathematical operator describing how the loss varies as you move the model's coefficients in different directions.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks
aliases: Gradient of the loss with respect to the weights

nodes.name: Derivative
nodes.definition: The slope a of the local linear approximation of a smooth, continuous function f at a point p; equivalently, the ratio epsilon_y / epsilon_x for small changes epsilon_x of the input.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Continuity
nodes.definition: The property that a small change in x can only result in a small change in y.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Smoothness
nodes.definition: The property that the curve of f has no abrupt angles, so that near any point it can be approximated by a straight line.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Local linear approximation
nodes.definition: The straight line of slope a that matches f around a point p: f(x + epsilon_x) = y + a * epsilon_x, valid only when x is close enough to p.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Optimization
nodes.definition: The task of finding values of x that minimize the value of f(x).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Loss as a function of the weights, f(W)
nodes.definition: With the inputs x and targets y_true held fixed, the chain y_pred = matmul(x, W); loss_value = loss(y_pred, y_true) is a function mapping weight values W to a scalar loss.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks
aliases: Loss as a function of the weights, f(W)

nodes.name: Partial derivative
nodes.definition: grad_ij: the derivative of loss_value = f(W) with respect to a single coefficient W[i, j], assuming all other coefficients are constant.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Step (scaling factor)
nodes.definition: A small scalar multiplying the gradient in the update W1 = W0 - step * grad(f(W0), W0).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Analytic minimization (and why it is intractable)
nodes.definition: Finding a minimum by solving derivative = 0 (grad(f(W), W) = 0 for a network) and comparing the candidate points.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks
aliases: Analytic minimization (and why it is intractable)

nodes.name: Mini-batch stochastic gradient descent (mini-batch SGD)
nodes.definition: The iterative training algorithm: draw a random batch, forward pass, compute the loss, compute the gradient of the loss with regard to the parameters (backward pass), move the parameters a little in the opposite direction from the gradient (W -= learning_rate * gradient).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Backward pass
nodes.definition: Computing the gradient of the loss with regard to the model's parameters (step 4 of the algorithm).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Batch size: true SGD, mini-batch, batch gradient descent
nodes.definition: The number of samples used per gradient update: one (true SGD), a mini-batch of reasonable size (mini-batch SGD), or all available data (batch gradient descent).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks
aliases: Batch size: true SGD, mini-batch, batch gradient descent

nodes.name: Local minimum
nodes.definition: A point on the loss curve where gradient descent with a small learning rate can get stuck because every small move increases the loss, even though lower points exist elsewhere.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Momentum
nodes.definition: Updating parameters based on the current gradient and on the previous update (velocity), by analogy with a ball rolling down the loss curve.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Chain rule
nodes.definition: The calculus identity for differentiating a composition of functions: if y = f(g(x)), the derivative of y with respect to x is the derivative of f (at g(x)) times the derivative of g (at x).
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks
aliases: Chain rule on a graph (path product)

nodes.name: A model as one nested function of its parameters
nodes.definition: Viewing the whole network plus loss as a single function of the weight tensors, obtained by nesting the atomic operations of each layer.

aliases: A model as one nested function of its parameters

nodes.name: Computation graph
nodes.definition: A directed acyclic graph of operations (tensor operations in deep learning) in which edges carry values from producing to consuming operations.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Automatic differentiation
nodes.definition: Generating the derivative of an expression automatically from its computation graph, rather than deriving it by hand.
nodes.chapter: 2 The mathematical building blocks of neural networks

nodes.name: Local (edge) derivative
nodes.definition: The derivative of one operation's output with respect to one of its inputs, evaluated at the forward-pass values; the label of a reversed edge.

nodes.name: Keras variable
nodes.definition: A mutable, trainable tensor created with keras.Variable(shape=..., initializer=...).

nodes.name: Weight initialization
nodes.definition: Choosing the starting values of parameters before training: here random uniform values for W and zeros for b.

nodes.name: Ambiguous features / inherent uncertainty

nodes.name: Overconfidence
nodes.definition: Predicting probabilities more extreme than warranted by the data, especially in ambiguous regions.

nodes.name: Interpolation (on the latent manifold)
nodes.definition: Morphing one input into another via a continuous path along which all points stay on the data manifold; used to make sense of unseen points from nearby seen points.

nodes.name: Linear interpolation in the encoding space

nodes.name: Latent manifold / latent space
nodes.definition: The low-dimensional, highly structured subspace of the potential input space where the data lives, which models need to fit.

nodes.name: Local generalization
nodes.definition: Generalization to inputs very close to what has been seen before, enabled by interpolation.

nodes.name: Extreme generalization
nodes.definition: The human ability to deal with extreme novelty, enabled by mechanisms other than interpolation: abstraction, symbolic world models, reasoning, logic, common sense, innate priors (reason).

nodes.name: Deep learning as manifold learning
nodes.definition: Viewing a deep learning model as a smooth high-dimensional curve fitted to data that lies on a latent manifold, so that the fitted curve approximates the manifold.

nodes.name: Architecture priors
nodes.definition: Constraints on the structure of the model curve that come from the model architecture.

nodes.name: Dense sampling of the input manifold

nodes.name: Data curation and feature engineering

nodes.name: Regularization

nodes.name: Hyperparameters vs parameters

nodes.name: Common-sense baseline
nodes.definition: The performance of a trivial strategy (random guessing, majority class, simplest non-ML technique) that a model must beat.

nodes.name: Class imbalance
nodes.definition: Unequal class frequencies in a dataset.

nodes.name: Data representativeness
nodes.definition: Training and test sets should each reflect the distribution of the data at hand.

nodes.name: Temporal leak
nodes.definition: Training a forecasting model on data from after the period it is evaluated on, typically caused by shuffling time-ordered data.

nodes.name: Redundancy between splits
nodes.definition: The same data point appearing in both training and validation/test sets.

nodes.name: Logistic regression (softmax regression)
nodes.definition: A linear classifier: class scores are an affine function of the input, converted to probabilities by a sigmoid (binary) or softmax (multiclass).

nodes.name: Dataset curation
nodes.definition: Making sure the dataset is appropriate: enough densely sampled data, minimal labeling errors, cleaned values, and only useful features.

nodes.name: Features and data efficiency
nodes.definition: Good features reduce how much data is needed, because the model no longer has to learn the representation itself.

nodes.name: Occam's razor
nodes.definition: Given two explanations, the simplest one, the one with fewer assumptions, is most likely correct.

nodes.name: Weight regularization
nodes.definition: Adding to the loss a cost associated with large weights, which forces the weights to stay small and regular.

nodes.name: L1 regularization
nodes.definition: A penalty proportional to the sum of the absolute values of the weights (the L1 norm).

nodes.name: L2 regularization / weight decay
nodes.definition: A penalty proportional to the sum of the squared weights. In neural networks it is called weight decay.

nodes.name: Dropout (introduced)
nodes.definition: A regularization technique from Hinton's group that randomly drops (zeroes) layer outputs during training.

nodes.name: Dropout rate
nodes.definition: The fraction of features zeroed out. The book gives a usual range of 0.2 to 0.5.

nodes.name: Training vs. inference behaviour
nodes.definition: Some layers compute differently during training and inference. Dropout is the first example in the book.

nodes.name: Conspiracies / co-adaptation
nodes.definition: Hinton's term for happenstance patterns encoded jointly by several units that are not significant in the data but fit the training sample.

nodes.name: Noise as a regularizer
nodes.definition: Injecting random perturbations into inputs or intermediate activations during training to prevent memorization of insignificant patterns.

nodes.name: Latent manifold
nodes.definition: The low-dimensional, structured subspace of input space on which real data lies.

nodes.name: Fit first, then regularize
nodes.definition: First obtain a model with some generalization power that can overfit; then improve generalization through regularization.

nodes.name: Problem framing
nodes.definition: Translating a business request into a precise ML problem: what data, what target, what task type, what constraints.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Baseline to beat
nodes.definition: A simple reference performance a model must exceed to demonstrate it has learned anything.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Types of machine learning tasks
nodes.definition: Categories such as binary/multiclass/multilabel classification, scalar/vector regression, segmentation, ranking, clustering, generation, reinforcement learning.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Matrix factorization (collaborative filtering)
nodes.definition: Recommendation by factoring the user–item interaction matrix into low-dimensional user and item vectors.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Deployment constraints
nodes.definition: Requirements such as privacy, latency, hardware or regulatory limits that restrict where and how a model is trained and run.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: The two framing hypotheses
nodes.definition: When you frame an ML task you implicitly assume (1) targets can be predicted from inputs and (2) your available data is informative enough to learn that relationship.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Predictive information in inputs
nodes.definition: The amount of information the inputs carry about the target; ML can only use what is present.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Label bias / bias laundering
nodes.definition: When labels encode human prejudice, a model trained on them reproduces that prejudice while appearing objective.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Data collection and annotation
nodes.definition: Acquiring raw inputs and producing their targets (often by manual labeling); the book calls it the most arduous, time-consuming and costly part of most ML projects.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Data annotation
nodes.definition: Producing target values (labels/tags) for inputs; either retrieved automatically or made by hand.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Data matters more than algorithms
nodes.definition: The observation that improving the dataset usually yields larger gains than improving the model.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Crowdsourced labeling
nodes.definition: Collecting labels from many online workers through a platform such as Mechanical Turk.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Representative training data
nodes.definition: Training data similar to the data the model will see in production.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Concept drift
nodes.definition: Change over time in production data properties that causes model accuracy to decay (full definition on p.201).
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Sampling bias
nodes.definition: A form of nonrepresentative data in which the data-collection process interacts with what you are trying to predict, producing biased measurements.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Target leaking
nodes.definition: Features in the training data that provide information about the targets but may not be available in production.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Measure of success
nodes.definition: The metric that defines project success; it guides all technical choices and should align with higher-level goals.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: ROC AUC
nodes.definition: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; the book lists it as common for balanced classification.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Precision and recall
nodes.definition: Metrics computed from true/false positives/negatives; recommended for imbalanced, ranking and multilabel problems.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Value normalization
nodes.definition: Rescaling input values so they are small and homogeneous, e.g., dividing by 255 or standardizing each feature to mean 0, std 1.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Missing-value handling
nodes.definition: Strategies for features whose values are unavailable for some samples: dropping the feature, adding a 'missing' category (categorical), imputing the mean or median or a model-predicted value (numerical), and training on synthesized missingness.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Statistical power (beating a baseline)
nodes.definition: In this book's workflow, the milestone of having a small model that beats a simple, common-sense baseline on validation data.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning
aliases: Statistical power and its two hypotheses

nodes.name: Last-layer activation
nodes.definition: The activation applied to a model's output layer, chosen so the output has the form the loss expects.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Hyperparameter tuning
nodes.definition: Searching over non-learned configuration choices (units per layer, learning rate, etc.), manually or with tools such as KerasTuner.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Setting stakeholder expectations
nodes.definition: Communicating before launch what the model can and cannot do, in terms non-specialists can act on.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: False-negative and false-positive rates
nodes.definition: FNR is the fraction of actual positives missed; FPR is the fraction of actual negatives wrongly flagged.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Decision threshold
nodes.definition: The probability cutoff that turns a classifier's score into a yes/no decision.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Inference model
nodes.definition: The form of a trained model used in production only to compute predictions, often exported out of Python and optimized for speed and memory.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: REST API deployment
nodes.definition: Serving a model on a server that receives inputs over HTTP and returns predictions.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Model export (SavedModel, ONNX)
nodes.definition: Writing a model's weights and computation graph outside the Python program so other runtimes can execute it.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Managed cloud model serving
nodes.definition: A third-party cloud service that hosts your uploaded model and provides an API endpoint.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: On-device (edge) deployment
nodes.definition: Running the model on the same device as the application: phone, embedded CPU, microcontroller, or local machine.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Efficiency–accuracy tradeoff
nodes.definition: Smaller, faster models generally achieve lower accuracy than the best large models.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: TensorFlow Lite
nodes.definition: A framework for efficient on-device deep learning inference.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: ONNX / ONNX runtime
nodes.definition: Open Neural Network Exchange, a portable model format, and its runtime.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: In-browser model deployment
nodes.definition: Running a model directly in the user's browser or desktop JavaScript app instead of on a server.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: TensorFlow.js
nodes.definition: TensorFlow's JavaScript library for running models in browsers and Electron apps.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Training-data leakage from models
nodes.definition: Recovering some information about the training data from a trained model.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Inference model optimization
nodes.definition: Shrinking or speeding up a trained model for prediction-only use.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Weight pruning
nodes.definition: Keeping only the most significant coefficients in weight tensors to lower parameter count.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Weight quantization
nodes.definition: Converting float32 weights to a lower-precision type such as int8 for inference.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Monitoring a deployed model
nodes.definition: Continuously tracking a model's behavior, performance on new data, integration and business impact after launch.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Randomized A/B testing
nodes.definition: Randomly routing some cases through the new model and a control subset through the old process, then comparing outcomes.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Model maintenance
nodes.definition: Planning for and building replacement model generations as deployed models decay.
nodes.chapter: 6 The universal workflow of machine learning

nodes.name: Collecting hard samples
nodes.definition: Prioritizing for annotation the samples the current model finds difficult to classify.

nodes.name: Progressive disclosure of complexity
nodes.definition: API design principle: easy to get started, arbitrarily complex use cases possible, with only incremental learning at each step.

nodes.name: Spectrum of Keras workflows
nodes.definition: The range of ways to build and train Keras models, each trading usability against flexibility.

nodes.name: Model subclassing
nodes.definition: Defining a model by subclassing keras.Model and writing the forward pass yourself.

nodes.name: Deferred weight creation (layer building)
nodes.definition: Keras layers create their weights at first call (or build()), once the input shape is known.

nodes.name: None as the batch dimension
nodes.definition: In a Keras shape, None marks an axis whose size is not fixed — by convention the batch axis.

nodes.name: keras.Input
nodes.definition: An object declaring the shape (per sample) and dtype of a model's input.

nodes.name: Naming models and layers
nodes.definition: Every Keras model and layer accepts a name argument.

nodes.name: Nonlinear topology
nodes.definition: A model graph that is not a single chain of layers.

nodes.name: Symbolic tensor
nodes.definition: An object that contains no data but encodes the shape and dtype of the tensors a model will process; it stands for future tensors of data.

nodes.name: Multi-input, multi-output model
nodes.definition: A model fed by several distinct inputs and producing several distinct outputs.

nodes.name: Concatenate layer
nodes.definition: A Keras layer that joins a list of tensors along an axis (by default the last).

nodes.name: Named inputs and outputs
nodes.definition: Inputs and output layers given a name= so data, losses and metrics can be passed as dicts keyed by name.

nodes.name: Layer connectivity (explicit graph)
nodes.definition: The record, kept by a Functional model, of which layer outputs feed which layers.

nodes.name: keras.utils.plot_model
nodes.definition: Utility that renders a model's layer graph to an image file.

nodes.name: Batch dimension (None)
nodes.definition: The leading axis of a tensor indexing samples; shown as None when unspecified.

nodes.name: Feature extraction (from a Functional model)
nodes.definition: Reusing intermediate layer outputs of a model as inputs or outputs of new models.

nodes.name: KerasTensor
nodes.definition: The symbolic tensor type returned by keras.Input and by layer calls on symbolic inputs.

nodes.name: Layer sharing between models
nodes.definition: Two models built from the same layer objects use the same weights.

nodes.name: Layer vs Model
nodes.definition: A layer is a building block for models; a model is the top-level object you train and export.

nodes.name: Structure matching for training
nodes.definition: Loss, metrics and targets must have the same structure as call()'s return value; inputs must have the structure call() expects.

nodes.name: Directed acyclic graph of layers
nodes.definition: A layer topology where data flows from inputs to outputs along directed edges without cycles.

nodes.name: Interoperability of model-building styles
nodes.definition: Sequential models, Functional models and subclassed layers or models can be nested inside each other freely.

nodes.name: Sigmoid vs. softmax output head
nodes.definition: For binary classification, one sigmoid unit outputs P(class 1). For multiclass, num_classes softmax units output a probability distribution.

nodes.name: Custom Keras metric
nodes.definition: A subclass of keras.metrics.Metric that defines state variables in __init__, updates them in update_state(), computes the value in result() and clears it in reset_state().

nodes.name: Stateful metric accumulation
nodes.definition: Computing a metric over many batches by accumulating sufficient statistics (sums, counts) rather than averaging per-batch values.

nodes.name: Root mean squared error
nodes.definition: The square root of the mean of squared differences between targets and predictions.

nodes.name: keras.ops
nodes.definition: Keras's backend-agnostic tensor operations namespace (NumPy-like functions plus neural-network ops).

nodes.name: Keras callback
nodes.definition: An object passed to fit() whose methods the model calls at various points during training.

nodes.name: Model checkpointing
nodes.definition: Saving the model's state at points during training, optionally only when it is the best so far.

nodes.name: Keras callback
nodes.definition: An object (subclass of keras.callbacks.Callback) passed to fit() in a list and invoked by the training loop at defined points (epoch/batch/training start and end).

nodes.name: Saving and loading models
nodes.definition: model.save(path) writes a full .keras archive; keras.models.load_model(path) restores it.

nodes.name: Custom callback
nodes.definition: A user subclass of keras.callbacks.Callback that overrides hook methods like on_epoch_begin/on_epoch_end.

nodes.name: Callback hook methods
nodes.definition: on_train_begin/end(logs), on_epoch_begin/end(epoch, logs), on_batch_begin/end(batch, logs).

nodes.name: logs dictionary
nodes.definition: Dict passed to every hook containing information about the previous batch, epoch or run, such as training and validation metrics.

nodes.name: Loop of progress
nodes.definition: The iterative cycle idea -> experiment -> results -> new idea (figure 7.6).

nodes.name: TensorBoard
nodes.definition: A visualization framework for processing experiment results, introduced here and described on p.237.

nodes.name: keras.callbacks.TensorBoard
nodes.definition: Built-in callback that writes training logs for TensorBoard to log_dir.

nodes.name: Supervised learning
nodes.definition: Setup with known targets associated with inputs, loss computed from targets and predictions.

nodes.name: Reinforcement learning
nodes.definition: Learning driven by occasional rewards.
aliases: Reinforcement learning from a self-contained environment

nodes.name: training argument (training vs. inference mode)
nodes.definition: Boolean argument of a layer's or model's call() that selects training-time or inference-time behaviour.

nodes.name: Trainable vs. non-trainable weights
nodes.definition: Trainable weights are updated by backpropagation to minimize the loss; non-trainable weights are updated by their owning layer during the forward pass.

nodes.name: Non-trainable weights
nodes.definition: Layer variables that the optimizer does not update. They may be updated during the forward pass.

nodes.name: Batch normalization (preview)
nodes.definition: A layer that normalizes activations. The book introduces it in chapter 9; here it is the one built-in layer with non-trainable weights.

nodes.name: Training step function
nodes.definition: A function that runs one gradient-descent update on one batch: forward pass, loss, gradients, optimizer update.

nodes.name: Backend-specific gradient retrieval
nodes.definition: Keras 3 has no backend-agnostic way to get gradients; each backend exposes its own autodiff API.

nodes.name: PyTorch autograd (define-by-run)
nodes.definition: PyTorch's autodiff: a one-time graph is built during each forward pass, and backward() fills .grad on tensors that require gradients.

nodes.name: Keras models as torch.nn.Module
nodes.definition: On the PyTorch backend, Keras layers and models inherit from torch.nn.Module and expose its API.

nodes.name: PyTorch training step for a Keras model
nodes.definition: forward → loss → loss.backward() → gather weight.value.grad → optimizer.apply under torch.no_grad() → model.zero_grad().

nodes.name: torch.no_grad() scope
nodes.definition: A context in which PyTorch does not record operations for autograd.

nodes.name: JAX statelessness
nodes.definition: JAX functions keep no persistent state; any state they use must be passed in, and any state they change must be returned.

nodes.name: Model.stateless_call()
nodes.definition: Keras's stateless forward pass: like call, but it takes trainable and non-trainable weights as inputs (and, per p.243, returns updated non-trainable weights).

nodes.name: Gradients via metaprogramming (JAX)
nodes.definition: Obtaining a gradient function by transforming a loss function, for example `jax.grad(loss_fn)`.

nodes.name: compute_loss_and_updates()
nodes.definition: The stateless JAX loss function for the training step. It returns (loss, updated non-trainable variables).

nodes.name: has_aux=True
nodes.definition: An option to jax.grad/value_and_grad declaring that the function returns (scalar, auxiliary), so only the scalar is differentiated.

nodes.name: Optimizer state (auxiliary variables)
nodes.definition: Variables an optimizer keeps across steps to speed up training, for example momentum buffers.

nodes.name: optimizer.stateless_apply()
nodes.definition: A pure optimizer update: (optimizer_variables, grads, trainable_variables) → (new trainable_variables, new optimizer_variables).

nodes.name: Training state as a function argument
nodes.definition: Bundling trainable, non-trainable and optimizer variables into one `state` tuple that train_step takes and returns.

nodes.name: Keras metric (low-level API)
nodes.definition: A stateful object that accumulates statistics with update_state() and reports with result().

nodes.name: SparseCategoricalAccuracy
nodes.definition: Fraction of samples where the argmax of the predicted class scores equals the integer target.

nodes.name: keras.metrics.Mean
nodes.definition: A metric that tracks the running average of scalar values.

nodes.name: Stateless metrics API (JAX)
nodes.definition: Methods stateless_update_state(variables, y_true, y_pred), stateless_result(variables) and stateless_reset_state() that take and return metric variables explicitly instead of mutating the metric.

nodes.name: Overriding train_step()
nodes.definition: Subclassing keras.Model and redefining train_step(), the method fit() calls for every batch, to implement a custom learning algorithm while still using fit().

nodes.name: Training state in a JAX train_step

aliases: Returning (logs, state) from a JAX train_step

nodes.definition: Keras metrics keep internal variables (e.g. total and count) that accumulate over batches; result() turns them into a value.

nodes.name: Auxiliary outputs with value_and_grad
nodes.definition: jax.value_and_grad(f, has_aux=True) returns ((value, aux), grads) for a function f returning (value, aux).

nodes.name: Convolutional neural network (ConvNet)
nodes.definition: A deep learning model built from convolution and pooling layers, used by most computer vision applications.

nodes.name: Conv2D layer
nodes.definition: A layer that applies learned filters of size kernel_size over local windows of its input.

nodes.name: MaxPooling2D layer
nodes.definition: Downsampling layer that keeps the maximum value in each pool_size x pool_size window.

nodes.name: GlobalAveragePooling2D
nodes.definition: Averages each channel over all spatial positions, turning (h, w, c) into a vector of length c.

nodes.name: Conv2D parameter count

nodes.name: channels_last vs channels_first
nodes.definition: Two conventions for where the channel axis goes in image tensors.

nodes.name: Feature map
nodes.definition: The spatial grid of activations produced by one filter (channel) of a convolution layer.

nodes.name: Relative error reduction
nodes.definition: The fraction by which the error rate shrinks: (e_old - e_new) / e_old.

nodes.name: Translation invariance
nodes.definition: The property that a pattern learned at one location is recognized at any location in the image.

nodes.name: Spatial hierarchy of patterns
nodes.definition: An organization of visual patterns where larger patterns are built out of smaller ones: edges -> parts -> objects.

nodes.name: Filter
nodes.definition: A learned pattern detector of a convolution layer; each filter produces one output channel.

nodes.name: Response map
nodes.definition: The 2D map output[:, :, n] showing how strongly filter n's pattern is present at each location of the input.

nodes.name: Window (kernel) size
nodes.definition: The height and width of the patches a convolution extracts; typically 3 × 3 or 5 × 5.

nodes.name: Convolution kernel
nodes.definition: The learned weight matrix that transforms each patch into an (output_depth,) vector, reused across every patch.

nodes.name: Spatial correspondence
nodes.definition: Each output location summarizes the corresponding location (neighbourhood) of the input.

nodes.name: Padding (preview)

nodes.name: Stride (preview)
nodes.definition: The distance between successive window positions, another reason output size can differ.

nodes.name: Border effect
nodes.definition: Shrinking of the output feature map because a window cannot be centred on tiles near the border without padding.

nodes.name: Downsampling
nodes.definition: Reducing the height and width of feature maps.

nodes.name: Receptive field
nodes.definition: The region of the input image that influences a given unit.

nodes.name: Average pooling
nodes.definition: Each local patch is replaced by the average value of each channel over the patch.
