nodes.definition: The empirical rule that a deep stack of narrow layers generally performs better than a shallow stack of large layers.
aliases: Deep and narrow vs. shallow and wide

nodes.name: Vanishing gradients
nodes.definition: The problem that, in a very deep chain of functions, error information backpropagated to early layers is overwhelmed by noise or becomes negligible, so those layers stop learning.

nodes.name: Ablation study
nodes.definition: Systematically removing parts of a system to find where its performance comes from.

nodes.name: 1 x 1 convolution projection
nodes.definition: A Conv2D layer with 1x1 kernels, used here with no activation to change the residual's number of channels (and, with strides, its spatial size).

nodes.name: padding='same'
nodes.definition: Padding mode that keeps height and width unchanged for stride-1 convolutions (and gives ceil(n/2) for 2x2 pooling).

nodes.name: Data normalization (standardization)
nodes.definition: Subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation so data is centered at 0 with unit variance.

nodes.name: Exponential moving average
nodes.definition: A running average updated as avg <- m*avg + (1-m)*new_value, where older values decay geometrically.

nodes.name: Internal covariate shift
nodes.definition: The change in the distribution of a hidden layer's inputs as earlier layers' parameters update during training.

nodes.name: Bias vector and use_bias=False
nodes.definition: The learned constant that makes Dense/Conv2D affine; it can be omitted when a normalization layer follows.

nodes.name: Depthwise separable convolution
nodes.definition: A convolution factored into a per-channel spatial (depthwise) convolution followed by a 1x1 pointwise convolution that mixes channels (SeparableConv2D in Keras).
aliases: When not to use separable convolution

nodes.name: cuDNN kernel
nodes.definition: An NVIDIA library routine implementing a deep learning operation, optimized down to individual machine instructions.

nodes.name: Co-evolution of hardware, software and algorithms
nodes.definition: The feedback loop in which GPUs/CUDA enabled backprop-trained ConvNets, which led NVIDIA to optimize for them, which consolidated research around them.
aliases: Co-evolution of hardware, software and algorithms

nodes.name: ConvNet architecture principles
nodes.definition: The chapter's checklist for designing ConvNets; the first two are on this page.

nodes.name: BN -> ReLU -> convolution ordering inside the block
nodes.definition: Each separable convolution is preceded by BatchNormalization and ReLU, so the block starts with normalization of its input.
aliases: BN -> ReLU -> convolution ordering inside the block

nodes.name: Parameter efficiency
nodes.definition: How much performance a model gets per trainable parameter.

nodes.name: Sigmoid output for binary classification
nodes.definition: A single Dense unit with sigmoid activation that outputs a probability in (0, 1) for the positive class.

nodes.name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
nodes.definition: A Transformer that processes an image as a sequence of patches; an alternative to ConvNets for computer vision.

nodes.name: Long-range relationships
nodes.definition: Dependencies between parts of the input that are far apart.

nodes.name: Interpretability
nodes.definition: Understanding why a model makes the decisions it makes.

nodes.name: Intermediate activation visualization
nodes.definition: Displaying the outputs of a model's convolution and pooling layers for a given input, channel by channel.

nodes.name: Filter visualization
nodes.definition: Showing the visual pattern each filter responds to most strongly.

nodes.name: Class activation heatmap
nodes.definition: A 2D grid of scores over an image indicating how important each location is for a given class.

nodes.name: Keras model summary
nodes.definition: A table of a model's layers with output shapes and parameter counts, plus totals.

nodes.name: Batch axis
nodes.definition: The leading dimension of a model input that indexes samples.

nodes.name: Single-image preprocessing
nodes.definition: Loading an image file, resizing it to the model's input size, converting to a float array and adding a batch axis.
aliases: Matching a pretrained model's input format

nodes.name: Multi-output model
nodes.definition: A Keras model that returns several output tensors for one input.

nodes.name: Displaying float images
nodes.definition: Converting an image array to uint8 before showing it with matplotlib.

nodes.name: Intermediate activation
nodes.definition: The output of a hidden layer (here a Conv2D or MaxPooling2D layer) for a particular input.

nodes.name: Non-determinism of learned filters
nodes.definition: Different training runs of the same architecture learn different specific filters, in different orders.

nodes.name: Per-channel normalization for display
nodes.definition: Rescaling each channel independently so its values fill a common display range, here via standardization, ×64, +128 and clipping to [0, 255].

nodes.name: Hierarchy of features with depth
nodes.definition: Convnet layers learn progressively more complex and abstract features: edges, then textures and parts, then class-related concepts.

nodes.name: Activation sparsity
nodes.definition: The share of channels (or units) that are zero for a given input; it increases with depth in this convnet.

nodes.name: Gradient ascent in input space
nodes.definition: Optimizing the input image, with the network's weights fixed, so as to maximize some activation.

nodes.name: KerasHub backbone and preset
nodes.definition: A pretrained feature-extractor network without its classification head, loaded with `Backbone.from_preset(name)`, which downloads configuration and weights.

nodes.name: Feature extractor sub-model
nodes.definition: A Keras model built from an existing model's input and one intermediate layer's output.

nodes.name: Filter-activation loss
nodes.definition: The mean activation of one filter (channel) of a chosen layer, over the batch and non-border positions; the objective maximized by gradient ascent.

nodes.name: Avoiding border artifacts
nodes.definition: Excluding activations near the edges of a feature map from the loss.

nodes.name: model.predict(x) vs model(x)
nodes.definition: predict batches the data and returns NumPy values (scalable, non-differentiable); calling the model returns backend tensors in memory (differentiable, not scalable).

nodes.name: Model-specific preprocessing
nodes.definition: Scaling input images exactly as during the model's pretraining.

nodes.name: L2 gradient normalization
nodes.definition: Dividing a gradient tensor by its L2 norm so that it has unit length, keeping only its direction.

nodes.name: model(x) vs model.predict(x)
nodes.definition: Two ways to run a Keras model: a direct differentiable call on tensors, and a batched, NumPy-returning, non-differentiable inference loop.

nodes.name: jax.grad function transformation
nodes.definition: A JAX transformation that maps a scalar-valued function f to a function computing the gradient of f with respect to its first argument.

nodes.name: Image deprocessing for display
nodes.definition: Converting an arbitrary float image tensor into a valid 8-bit image by standardizing, rescaling to a target mean and spread, clipping, cropping and casting.

nodes.name: Image grid (montage) construction
nodes.definition: Pasting many equally sized images into a larger array at regular offsets, separated by margins.

nodes.name: Filter bank
nodes.definition: The collection of filters learned by one layer; its outputs describe the input as a vector of responses to each filter.

nodes.name: Fourier-transform analogy
nodes.definition: The comparison between a layer expressing its input in terms of its filters and the Fourier transform expressing a signal as a combination of cosines.

nodes.name: Grad-CAM
nodes.definition: Gradient-weighted class activation mapping: weighting each channel of a conv layer's output feature map by the gradient of the class score with respect to that channel, then aggregating into a heatmap.

nodes.name: Model interpretability
nodes.definition: Understanding and explaining why a model makes the predictions it makes.

nodes.name: KerasHub task API
nodes.definition: High-level KerasHub classes for end-to-end workflows that wrap preprocessing, a feature-extraction network and a task-specific head into one model.

nodes.name: Backbone vs full pretrained classifier
nodes.definition: A backbone is the pretrained feature extractor without the classification head; the full classifier adds the head that outputs scores for the original training classes (here the 1,000 ImageNet classes).

nodes.name: Splitting a model at an intermediate layer
nodes.definition: Building one model from the original input to an intermediate layer's output, and a second model from that output to the final prediction.
aliases: Re-applying head layers to a new input
Splitting a model at an intermediate layer

nodes.name: Task preprocessor
nodes.definition: The preprocessing layer included in a KerasHub task, applied automatically by predict().

nodes.name: Backend-specific gradient code in Keras 3
nodes.definition: Keras models and keras.ops run on TensorFlow, PyTorch or JAX, but gradient computation in custom code uses each backend's own API.

nodes.name: Leaf tensor with requires_grad (PyTorch)
nodes.definition: A tensor not produced by a tracked operation, whose .grad attribute is populated by backward() when requires_grad is True.

nodes.name: Channel importance weights (pooled gradients)
nodes.definition: One number per channel: the average over batch and spatial positions of the gradient of the class with respect to that channel.

nodes.name: Heatmap post-processing
nodes.definition: Clipping negative values to 0 and dividing by the maximum so the heatmap lies in [0, 1].

nodes.name: Colormap lookup table
nodes.definition: A table of 256 RGB colors indexed by an 8-bit intensity value.

nodes.name: Projection to 2D (dimensionality reduction)
nodes.definition: Mapping high-dimensional activation vectors to 2D points while keeping as much of their organization as possible.

nodes.name: Penultimate (second-before-last) layer
nodes.definition: The layer immediately before the classification layer, the book's recommended target for latent space visualization.

nodes.name: Intrinsic dimensionality
nodes.definition: The number of independent degrees of freedom of the manifold that data points lie on, as opposed to the number of coordinates (ambient dimension) used to write them down.

nodes.name: Hierarchy of ConvNet filters
nodes.definition: Earlier layers learn filters for edges and basic textures; later layers learn increasingly abstract concepts.

nodes.name: The three essential computer vision tasks
nodes.definition: Image classification, image segmentation, and object detection, which the book says nearly all vision applications reduce to (p.334).
aliases: The three essential computer vision tasks

nodes.name: Image classification
nodes.definition: Assigning one or more labels to an entire image, either single-label (mutually exclusive) or multilabel (all categories that apply).

nodes.name: Image segmentation
nodes.definition: Partitioning an image into areas, each usually representing a category, at pixel-level precision.

nodes.name: Object detection
nodes.definition: Drawing bounding boxes around objects of interest and assigning each box a class.

nodes.name: Bounding box
nodes.definition: A rectangle drawn around an object of interest.

nodes.name: Semantic segmentation
nodes.definition: Each pixel is independently classified into a semantic category; instances of the same class are not distinguished.

nodes.name: Instance segmentation
nodes.definition: Segmentation that parses out individual object instances, separating, for example, cat 1 from cat 2.

nodes.name: Panoptic segmentation
nodes.definition: Assigns each pixel both a semantic label and an instance label; the most informative of the three types.

nodes.name: Segmentation mask
nodes.definition: The segmentation equivalent of a label: an image the same size as the input, with a single color channel, where each integer value is the class of the corresponding pixel.

nodes.name: Oxford-IIIT Pets dataset
nodes.definition: A dataset of 7,390 pictures of various breeds of cats and dogs, with a segmentation mask for each picture.

nodes.name: Aligning inputs and targets by sorted filenames
nodes.definition: Pairing each input with its target by sorting two path lists whose files share names.
aliases: Aligning inputs and targets by sorted filenames

nodes.name: Rescaling class ids for visualization
nodes.definition: Mapping small integer labels to widely spaced intensities so different classes are visually distinguishable.

nodes.name: Aligned shuffling of paired lists
nodes.definition: Applying the same random permutation to two lists that must stay in correspondence.

nodes.name: Zero-based integer class labels
nodes.definition: Class ids encoded as integers 0..K-1, as expected by sparse categorical cross-entropy.

nodes.name: Encoder-decoder segmentation ConvNet
nodes.definition: A ConvNet that first downsamples an image into compact feature maps and then upsamples them back to the input resolution to produce per-pixel outputs.

nodes.name: Strided convolution
nodes.definition: A convolution whose window moves by more than one pixel per step, downsampling the output.

nodes.name: Transposed convolution (Conv2DTranspose)
nodes.definition: A convolution-like layer that learns to upsample feature maps, inverting the spatial shape change of a strided convolution.

nodes.name: Per-pixel softmax
nodes.definition: A softmax applied independently at every spatial position over the class channels.

nodes.name: Intersection over Union (IoU)
nodes.definition: The ratio of the overlap area to the combined area of predicted and ground-truth masks for a class.

nodes.name: Per-pixel argmax decoding
nodes.definition: Converting a (H, W, C) probability map into a (H, W) class map by picking, for each pixel, the class with the highest probability.

nodes.name: Segment Anything Model (SAM)
nodes.definition: A large pretrained, promptable segmentation model released by Meta AI in April 2023, trained on 11 million images with over 1 billion masks.

nodes.name: Promptable (class-agnostic) segmentation
nodes.definition: Segmentation where the target object is specified at inference time by a prompt rather than by a fixed class output.

nodes.name: KerasHub tasks and presets
nodes.definition: KerasHub provides pretrained architectures with weights; tasks such as `ImageClassifier` and `ImageSegmenter` wrap them into end-to-end models loaded with `from_preset`.

nodes.name: Model-assisted data labeling (feedback loop)
nodes.definition: Building a dataset and a model together: a partially trained model helps annotate data, which trains an improved model.

nodes.name: Image encoder
nodes.definition: The component mapping an input image to a much smaller image embedding.

nodes.name: Prompt encoder
nodes.definition: Maps prompts (points or boxes) to an embedded vector.

nodes.name: Mask decoder
nodes.definition: Takes the image embedding and the prompt embedding and outputs a few possible predicted masks.

nodes.name: Sampling prompts from masks
nodes.definition: Generating training prompts from ground-truth masks: a random pixel inside the mask (point) or the box around the mask (box).

nodes.name: Joint (end-to-end) training
nodes.definition: Training all components of a model together from a single objective.

nodes.name: Aspect-ratio-preserving resize with padding (letterboxing)
nodes.definition: Scaling an image uniformly so its longest side equals the target size, then padding the shorter side with a constant to reach a square input.

nodes.name: Labeled point prompts
nodes.definition: Prompts given as pixel coordinates with labels: 1 for foreground (include) and 0 for background (exclude).

nodes.name: Box prompts
nodes.definition: An approximate rectangle around the object, which SAM refines into a precise mask.

nodes.name: RGBA mask overlay
nodes.definition: Displaying a binary mask as a semi-transparent colored layer on top of an image.

nodes.name: Thresholding mask logits
nodes.definition: Turning real-valued per-pixel scores into a boolean mask by comparing them to a threshold, here 0.0.

nodes.name: Mask overlay visualization
nodes.definition: Drawing a semi-transparent coloured mask on top of an image to inspect a segmentation.

nodes.name: Prompt ambiguity and multi-mask output
nodes.definition: A prompt can correspond to several valid segmentations; SAM addresses this by returning several candidate masks.

nodes.name: Model-assisted annotation
nodes.definition: Using a model's predictions as a starting point that humans verify or correct when building labeled datasets.

nodes.name: Two-stage detector (R-CNN)
nodes.definition: A detector that first extracts region proposals and then classifies each proposal with a ConvNet.

nodes.name: Single-stage detector
nodes.definition: A detector that predicts boxes and labels jointly with a single deep learning model.

nodes.name: Region proposal
nodes.definition: A candidate bounding box around an object-like area, produced by the first stage of an R-CNN.

nodes.name: Heuristic
nodes.definition: "A bundle of hard-coded rules someone made up" — the book's definition.

nodes.name: YOLO (You Only Look Once)
nodes.definition: A family of single-stage detectors, the first from 2015; 12 versions existed at the time of writing.

nodes.name: COCO dataset
nodes.definition: Common Objects in Context: real-world photos with human-created labels, bounding boxes and segmentation masks.

nodes.name: Aspect-preserving box normalization
nodes.definition: Scaling box coordinates by 1/max(W, H) and offsetting the shorter axis by half the size difference.
aliases: Aspect-preserving image placement on the unit square

nodes.name: Golden-ratio hue generation
nodes.definition: Assigning the k-th label the hue (0.618·k) mod 1 at fixed saturation and value.

nodes.name: Box confidence score
nodes.definition: A scalar predicted with each box, trained to be high when an object is present at that grid location and zero otherwise.

nodes.name: ConvNet backbone
nodes.definition: A (usually pretrained) convolutional network used as a feature extractor, onto which task-specific layers are attached.

nodes.name: Shuffling training data
nodes.definition: Randomly permuting the training samples so that each batch is representative of the whole dataset.

nodes.name: Class probability map
nodes.definition: A grid-shaped output that gives, for each grid cell, a probability distribution over the object labels.

nodes.name: Matching preprocessing (ImageConverter)
nodes.definition: A KerasHub layer, loaded from the same preset as the model, that resizes and rescales raw images to the format the pretrained model expects.

nodes.name: YOLO detection head
nodes.definition: The layers added on top of the backbone that convert its feature maps into per-grid-cell box and class predictions.

nodes.name: YOLO box encoding
nodes.definition: Each box is represented by the cell containing its center plus (x, y, w, h): the center's offset within that cell (0 to 1) and the box's width and height relative to the image.

nodes.name: No locality constraint in the YOLO head
nodes.definition: Because the head flattens the feature map into dense layers, each grid cell's prediction depends on the entire image's features.
aliases: No locality constraint in the YOLO head

nodes.name: Trainable vs. non-trainable parameters
nodes.definition: Trainable parameters are updated by gradient descent; non-trainable ones are model state not updated by gradients.

nodes.name: YOLO training targets
nodes.definition: Per image, a `(S, S)` integer class map and a `(S, S, 5)` box array with the grid-encoded box and confidence 1 in each box's center cell, zeros elsewhere.

nodes.name: Visualizing targets before training
nodes.definition: Drawing the encoded labels back onto the input image to check that the data preparation is correct.

nodes.name: Confidence cutoff
nodes.definition: A threshold below which predicted boxes are not drawn (or not reported).

nodes.name: Per-output losses
nodes.definition: In a multi-output Keras model, each output gets its own loss and Keras sums them into one training objective.

nodes.name: YOLO box loss
nodes.definition: Sum-squared error between target and predicted box parameters, counted only in grid cells that contain an object, plus a confidence term whose target reflects box quality.

nodes.name: Intersection over Union (IoU)
nodes.definition: Ratio of the area where two regions overlap to the area they cover together.

nodes.name: Loss term weighting
nodes.definition: Multiplying individual terms of a composite loss by constants to balance their influence on gradients.

nodes.name: Sign-preserving square root
nodes.definition: sign(x) * sqrt(|x|), here with a small epsilon inside the root.

nodes.name: Masking with ops.where
nodes.definition: Selecting element-wise between two tensors using a boolean condition to zero out or reweight parts of a loss.

nodes.name: Per-sample loss values
nodes.definition: A custom loss returns one value per example; Keras reduces these over the batch.

nodes.name: Confidence cutoff
nodes.definition: A threshold on a detector's confidence score; only predictions at or above it are reported.

nodes.name: Argmax decoding of class maps
nodes.definition: Turning per-cell class probability vectors into a single predicted label per cell by taking the index of the maximum.

nodes.name: RetinaNet
nodes.definition: A single-stage object detector following the same basic principles as YOLO, used pretrained in section 12.3.

nodes.name: Feature pyramid network (FPN)
nodes.definition: An architecture that turns a backbone's multi-resolution features into a pyramid of semantically strong maps by top-down upsampling and lateral summation with same-size backbone maps.

nodes.name: Lateral connection
nodes.definition: A connection that sums an upsampled top-down feature map with the backbone feature map of the same size.

nodes.name: Resolution vs. semantics trade-off
nodes.definition: In a ConvNet, early layers have high spatial resolution but low-level features; later layers have rich semantics but low resolution.

nodes.name: Out-of-distribution input
nodes.definition: An input that differs systematically from the training data.

nodes.name: Bounding-box format
nodes.definition: The convention used to encode a rectangle with four numbers, e.g. corners (xyxy), top-left plus size (xywh), centre plus size, in pixels or relative to the image.

nodes.name: Padded detection outputs and num_detections
nodes.definition: Returning a fixed maximum number of detections per image (here 100) plus a count of how many are valid.

nodes.name: Out-of-distribution generalization
nodes.definition: A model's ability to perform well on inputs that differ systematically from its training data.

nodes.name: Timeseries
nodes.definition: Any data obtained via measurements at regular intervals.

nodes.name: Timeseries forecasting
nodes.definition: Predicting what happens next in a timeseries from its past.

nodes.name: Anomaly detection
nodes.definition: Detecting anything unusual in a continuous data stream.

nodes.name: Event detection
nodes.definition: Identifying occurrences of a specific, expected event in a continuous stream.

nodes.name: Timeseries dynamics
nodes.definition: The behaviour of a system over time: periodic cycles, trends, regular regime and sudden spikes.

nodes.name: Jena Climate dataset
nodes.definition: Weather measurements from the Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry in Jena: 14 quantities every 10 minutes, 2009–2016 subset, 420,551 records.

nodes.name: Multivariate timeseries array layout
nodes.definition: A 2D array with time along the first axis and variables along the second.

nodes.name: Periodicity
nodes.definition: Regular repetition of a pattern over time, at one or more timescales.

nodes.name: Exploratory plotting
nodes.definition: Visualizing raw data before modeling to understand its structure.

nodes.name: Chronological (temporal) train/validation/test split
nodes.definition: Splitting a timeseries into contiguous blocks ordered in time: training first, then validation, then test.

nodes.name: Sliding-window samples
nodes.definition: Turning one long series into many training samples by extracting fixed-length windows at successive offsets.

nodes.name: keras.utils.timeseries_dataset_from_array
nodes.definition: A Keras utility that builds a Dataset of windows (sequences) and optional targets from an array, on the fly.

nodes.name: Forecast horizon and target offset
nodes.definition: How far after the input window the target lies, implemented as an index offset between data and targets.

nodes.name: Batch of timeseries samples
nodes.definition: A group of windows processed together in one gradient step.

nodes.name: Commonsense (non-learning) baseline
nodes.definition: A trivial, hand-specified prediction rule used as a reference score and sanity check before training models.

nodes.name: Imbalanced classification
nodes.definition: Classification where class frequencies differ greatly.

nodes.name: Architecture prior
nodes.definition: Structural assumptions in a model that shape what it can learn easily.

nodes.name: MaxPooling1D
nodes.definition: Downsampling of a sequence by taking the maximum over windows.

nodes.name: Recurrent neural network
nodes.definition: A network that processes sequence elements in order while maintaining a state that summarizes what it has seen so far.
aliases: RNN as a causal sequence model
Recurrent neural network as a hardcoded loop
Recurrent neural network: forgetting over long sequences

nodes.name: LSTM layer
nodes.definition: Long Short-Term Memory recurrent layer, long very popular among RNN variants.

nodes.name: Order information
nodes.definition: Information carried by the temporal arrangement of observations.

nodes.name: Feedforward network
nodes.definition: A network without memory: each input is processed independently with no state kept between inputs.

nodes.name: State of an RNN
nodes.definition: An internal vector carrying information about the sequence elements processed so far.

nodes.name: Simple RNN step function
nodes.definition: The step output_t = activation(dot(W, input_t) + dot(U, state_t) + b), with two weight matrices and one bias vector.

nodes.name: Step function
nodes.definition: The per-timestep computation that characterizes an RNN; for the simple RNN, tanh(W·input_t + U·state_t + b).

nodes.name: Unrolling an RNN over time
nodes.definition: Representing the recurrent loop as a chain of identical cells, one per timestep, connected through the state.

nodes.name: return_sequences
nodes.definition: Constructor argument of Keras recurrent layers choosing between full output sequences and only the last output.

nodes.name: Variable-length inputs (timesteps=None)
nodes.definition: Declaring the timesteps axis as None in keras.Input so the model accepts sequences of any length.

nodes.name: Stacking recurrent layers
nodes.definition: Placing several recurrent layers in sequence, each consuming the previous one's full output sequence.

nodes.name: GRU
nodes.definition: The third Keras recurrent layer, also designed to address SimpleRNN's issues.

nodes.name: LSTM carry track (C_t)
nodes.definition: An additional dataflow in the LSTM that carries information across timesteps, parallel to the sequence.

nodes.name: i_t, f_t, k_t transformations
nodes.definition: Three transformations of SimpleRNN form, each with its own weights (Wi, Ui, bi; Wf, Uf, bf; Wk, Uk, bk).

nodes.name: Recurrent dropout
nodes.definition: A dropout variant for recurrent layers, listed on this page as the first technique to fight overfitting in RNNs.

nodes.name: Temporally constant dropout mask
nodes.definition: A dropout mask sampled once and reused at every timestep of a sequence.

nodes.name: cuDNN kernel
nodes.definition: A highly optimized, low-level, NVIDIA-provided implementation of an algorithm such as LSTM or GRU, used by Keras on GPU with default arguments.

nodes.name: Model capacity
nodes.definition: The representational power of a model, increased by more units per layer or more layers.

nodes.name: Bidirectional RNN
nodes.definition: Two regular RNNs (e.g. GRU or LSTM) processing the same input sequence chronologically and antichronologically, with their representations merged.

nodes.name: Order dependence of RNNs
nodes.definition: RNNs process timesteps in order, so shuffling or reversing them can completely change the representations extracted.

nodes.name: Ensembling (preview)
nodes.definition: Combining different models or representations to boost performance.

nodes.name: Order sensitivity vs. direction invariance
nodes.definition: Data where order matters but the reading direction does not (text) suits bidirectional models. Data where recency dominates (weather) does not.

nodes.name: Information ceiling of a dataset
nodes.definition: The best achievable performance is limited by how much the inputs reveal about the target, whatever the model.

nodes.name: Information arbitrage
nodes.definition: Gaining a trading advantage by using data or insights other market participants are missing.

nodes.name: Applicability of ML forecasting
nodes.definition: ML forecasting works on data where the past is a good predictor of the future.

nodes.name: Natural language processing (NLP)
nodes.definition: Using computers to interpret and manipulate human language (defined on p.406).

nodes.name: Text classification
nodes.definition: Predicting a category for an input text.

nodes.name: Statistical / learned NLP
nodes.definition: NLP based on models that learn parameters from data (starting with logistic regression) instead of hand-written rules.

nodes.name: Language modeling
nodes.definition: Predicting which word will likely come next given an incomplete sentence.

nodes.name: NLP as pattern recognition
nodes.definition: Modern NLP is pattern recognition applied to words, as computer vision is pattern recognition applied to pixels.

nodes.name: Token
nodes.definition: A small individual unit of text produced by the splitting step.

nodes.name: Regular expression
nodes.definition: A pattern language that flexibly matches sequences of characters in text; the book uses it to split strings into tokens.

nodes.name: Character-level vs. word-level representation
nodes.definition: Two ways to make text numeric: give each character a unique index (as ASCII does), or split on spaces and punctuation and give each word a unique index.

nodes.name: Indexing
nodes.definition: Mapping each token to a unique integer index.

nodes.name: Vocabulary
nodes.definition: A mapping from specific tokens occurring in the training data to integer indices.

nodes.name: Unknown token [UNK] / out-of-vocabulary handling
nodes.definition: A reserved vocabulary entry to which every token not in the vocabulary is mapped.

nodes.name: Text standardization
nodes.definition: Text-to-text normalization that erases encoding differences you don't want the model to deal with; the book calls it a basic form of feature engineering.

nodes.name: Stemming / lemmatization
nodes.definition: Mapping words to a common root, traditionally with regular expressions, e.g. "tired" -> "tire", "trophies" -> "trophy".

nodes.name: Tokenizer
nodes.definition: An object that maps text to a sequence of token indices.

nodes.name: Vocabulary size and parameter count
nodes.definition: The book notes that limiting vocabulary size is an important way to limit the number of parameters in a model.

nodes.name: Frequency-ordered vocabulary
nodes.definition: In these vocabularies, index order is frequency rank because tokens are appended from most_common.

nodes.name: Word-level tokenization
nodes.definition: Splitting text into words (and here, the punctuation marks . , ! ? ;) and giving each distinct word its own ID.

nodes.name: Character-level tokenization
nodes.definition: Splitting text into individual characters, each with its own ID.

nodes.name: Subword tokenization
nodes.definition: Tokenization with units between characters and words: frequent words stay whole, rare words are split into frequent pieces.

nodes.name: Out-of-vocabulary token "[UNK]"
nodes.definition: A reserved vocabulary entry (index 0 here) for every token not in the vocabulary.

nodes.name: Tokenization as compression
nodes.definition: Viewing a tokenizer as a code that should represent text with few tokens, each drawn from a small vocabulary.

nodes.name: Byte-pair encoding (BPE)
nodes.definition: A subword tokenization algorithm that starts from single characters and repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent symbol pair into a new symbol, adding it to the vocabulary.

nodes.name: Character-split word counts
nodes.definition: The BPE starting state: a mapping from each distinct word, written as space-separated characters, to its frequency in the corpus.

nodes.name: Merge rule
nodes.definition: A learned instruction 'replace adjacent symbols A B with AB', together with the order (rank) in which it was learned.

nodes.name: Regex lookarounds for whole-symbol matching
nodes.definition: (?<!\S) asserts that the preceding character isn't a non-space (so it is a space or the string start); (?!\S) asserts the same for the following character.

nodes.name: Overlapping regex matches
nodes.definition: Returning every match even when matches share characters; offered by the third-party regex module via overlapped=True.

nodes.name: Choosing a tokenization technique
nodes.definition: Deciding between character, word and subword tokenization for a problem.

nodes.name: Categorical feature
nodes.definition: A feature whose values come from a predefined set without numeric meaning.

nodes.name: Bag-of-words (set) model
nodes.definition: A model that treats text as an unordered set of tokens.

nodes.name: Sequence model
nodes.definition: A model that takes the order of input tokens into account; the book names RNNs and Transformers.

nodes.name: Word-position information (positional encoding)
nodes.definition: Information about each token's position, added to its representation so an order-agnostic model can use order.

nodes.name: Unlabeled data
nodes.definition: Examples without target labels, here the reviews in unsup/.

nodes.name: Inspecting the data before modeling
nodes.definition: The practice of looking at raw samples before designing or training a model.

nodes.name: Per-class (stratified) split
nodes.definition: Splitting each class separately with the same fraction, so every split keeps the original class proportions.

nodes.name: Seeded shuffling for reproducibility
nodes.definition: Using a random generator with a fixed seed so that the shuffle, and therefore the split, is the same every run.

nodes.name: Noise in raw text
nodes.definition: Artifacts in real-world text, such as markup, misspellings and inconsistent casing, that a model's preprocessing must handle.

nodes.name: Out-of-vocabulary ([UNK]) token
nodes.definition: A reserved vocabulary entry that all unknown words map to.

nodes.name: text_dataset_from_directory
nodes.definition: A Keras utility that creates a batched tf.data.Dataset of (text, label) pairs from a directory with one subfolder per class.

nodes.name: TextVectorization layer
nodes.definition: A Keras preprocessing layer that standardizes, splits and indexes text and can output integer sequences or encodings such as multi-hot.

nodes.name: adapt() for preprocessing layers
nodes.definition: Computing a preprocessing layer's internal state from a dataset before training.

nodes.name: Preprocessing inside tf.data with map
nodes.definition: Applying a function, here the vectorization layer, to every element of a Dataset, optionally in parallel.

nodes.name: Preprocessing as the bottleneck
nodes.definition: For small models, turning raw text into tensors can take longer than the training update itself.

nodes.name: Input-pipeline bottleneck
nodes.definition: The situation where the CPU-side preparation of batches is slower than the accelerator's training step, so the accelerator waits.

nodes.name: tf.data pipelines
nodes.definition: A streaming data API whose Dataset objects support parallel map, batching, caching and prefetching.

nodes.name: n-gram
nodes.definition: An ordered sequence of n consecutive tokens; unigrams (n=1) and bigrams (n=2) are the common cases.

nodes.name: Reusing the model, changing the features
nodes.definition: Keeping build_linear_classifier fixed and changing only the input encoding.
aliases: Reusing the model, changing the features

nodes.name: Learned features vs. engineered features
nodes.definition: Letting the model learn representations from raw input instead of designing features by hand.

nodes.name: Cosine and L2 distance
nodes.definition: Measures of how far apart two vectors are: the angle-based cosine distance and the Euclidean L2 distance.

nodes.name: Meaningful directions (vector arithmetic)
nodes.definition: Consistent displacement vectors that encode a relation, so that adding the vector maps one word to its related word.

nodes.name: Keras Embedding layer
nodes.definition: A layer that maps integer token indices to dense vectors via a trainable lookup table.

nodes.name: Task-specific embedding spaces
nodes.definition: The idea that the best embedding geometry depends on the task, so embeddings are often learned per task.

nodes.name: Masking padded timesteps
nodes.definition: Marking sequence positions that should be ignored (typically padding) so that downstream layers skip them.

nodes.name: Pretraining
nodes.definition: Training a component, here the word embedding, separately on more data and without task labels, then reusing it.

nodes.name: Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW)
nodes.definition: An unsupervised setup that slides a window over text and predicts each window's middle word from the surrounding words.

nodes.name: Unsupervised (self-supervised) pretraining task
nodes.definition: A training objective built from unlabeled data, where the target is part of the input itself.

nodes.name: Context window
nodes.definition: A span of consecutive tokens around a target position; here nine tokens with the middle one as label.

nodes.name: Caching preprocessed data
nodes.definition: Storing the output of a deterministic input pipeline after the first epoch so later epochs reuse it.

nodes.name: Preprocessing-bound training
nodes.definition: A training run where the CPU input pipeline, not the accelerator, limits speed.

nodes.name: Data-constrained model
nodes.definition: A model whose accuracy is limited by the amount of training data rather than by its capacity.

nodes.name: Set-based (bag-of-words / n-gram) models
nodes.definition: Models that use only the presence or absence of tokens or n-grams.

nodes.name: Detokenization
nodes.definition: Mapping a sequence of integer token IDs back to string tokens and joining them into text.

nodes.name: Combinatorial explosion of output sequences
nodes.definition: The number of possible length-L sequences over a vocabulary of size V is V^L, which grows exponentially with L.

nodes.name: Shifted-by-one targets (next-token labels)
nodes.definition: The training target sequence for a causal language model is the input sequence offset by one token, so the label at each position is the following token.

nodes.name: Autoregressive generation
nodes.definition: Producing a sequence by repeatedly predicting the next token and feeding each prediction back to the model as the next input.

nodes.name: Reusing trained weights in a differently shaped model
nodes.definition: Building an inference model with the same layer configuration as a training model and copying the trained parameters into it with `set_weights(get_weights())`.
aliases: Reusing trained weights in a differently shaped model

nodes.name: Prompt
nodes.definition: A snippet of text fed to the model before it begins predicting new tokens.

nodes.name: Priming the state with a prompt
nodes.definition: Running the prompt tokens through a recurrent model one at a time, carrying the state, so the model's state encodes the prompt before generation.
aliases: Priming the state with a prompt

nodes.name: Greedy decoding
nodes.definition: At each generation step, select the token with the highest predicted probability.

nodes.name: Vocabulary lookup tables
nodes.definition: Dictionaries mapping each vocabulary string to its integer index and back.

nodes.name: Causality in language-model training
nodes.definition: The requirement that the prediction at position t uses only tokens at positions up to t, never future tokens.

nodes.name: Training versus inference in language models
nodes.definition: During training the model is fed the true previous tokens in parallel; during inference it must be run in a loop on its own predictions.
aliases: Training versus inference in language models

nodes.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
nodes.definition: Modeling problems where a source sequence is mapped to a generated target sequence, such as translation or question answering.

nodes.name: Encoder-decoder architecture
nodes.definition: A seq2seq model made of an encoder that represents the source sequence and a decoder that generates the target sequence conditioned on that representation.

nodes.name: [start] and [end] tokens
nodes.definition: Special tokens added to target sequences: [start] seeds generation and [end] signals that generation should stop.

nodes.name: Training on the shifted true target
nodes.definition: Feeding the decoder the true previous target tokens during training rather than its own predictions.
aliases: Training on the shifted true target

nodes.name: Start and end tokens
nodes.definition: Marker tokens that signal the start and end of a generated sequence.

nodes.name: Custom standardization function
nodes.definition: A callable passed to TextVectorization(standardize=...) that normalizes raw strings before splitting.

nodes.name: Sample weights for padded targets
nodes.definition: Per-position weights so padded label positions are ignored in loss and metrics.

nodes.name: Sample weights as a padding mask
nodes.definition: A per-token weight tensor, here `labels != 0`, that multiplies each position's loss and metric contribution, so padded positions contribute nothing.
aliases: Sample weights as a padding mask

nodes.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
nodes.definition: Mapping a source sequence to a target sequence of possibly different length, such as an English sentence to a Spanish one.

nodes.name: Fixed-size state bottleneck
nodes.definition: In an RNN encoder-decoder, all information about the source must pass through one fixed-size vector.

nodes.name: Causal decoder versus bidirectional encoder
nodes.definition: The decoder must not see future target tokens, while the encoder may freely use the whole source.

nodes.name: Conditioning via `initial_state`
nodes.definition: Passing the encoder's output as the decoder GRU's starting hidden state: `rnn_layer(x, initial_state=encoder_output)`.

nodes.name: Next-token (teacher-forced) accuracy
nodes.definition: The share of non-padding target positions where the model's top prediction equals the true next token, given the true previous tokens.

nodes.name: Train/inference mismatch (exposure bias)
nodes.definition: During training the decoder sees ground-truth prefixes. At inference it sees its own, possibly wrong, outputs.

nodes.name: BLEU score
nodes.definition: A machine-translation metric that measures n-gram overlap between a candidate translation and one or more reference translations.

nodes.name: Parameter budget of the RNN translator
nodes.definition: The breakdown of the 34,869,912 parameters across layers.
aliases: Parameter budget of the RNN translator

nodes.name: Encoder state bottleneck
nodes.definition: In a plain RNN encoder-decoder, the entire source sequence must be compressed into one fixed-size state vector that initializes the decoder.

nodes.name: Attention (as introduced here)
nodes.definition: A mechanism that lets a model pull information from any position in a sequence, weighted by contextual relevance.

nodes.name: Selective and contextual retrieval
nodes.definition: Pulling only the relevant pieces of a large body of information, with relevance determined by the current task.

nodes.name: Einsum notation
nodes.definition: A way to specify array operations by labelling each input axis with a letter and writing input1,input2->output; repeated letters are multiplied, letters missing from the output are summed over.

nodes.name: Attention scoring (setup)
nodes.definition: Giving the model a way to score every source vector by its relevance to the current target word.

nodes.name: keras.ops.einsum and EinsumDense
nodes.definition: The two ways to use einsums in Keras: a backend-agnostic function and a Dense layer whose matmul is an einsum.

nodes.name: Attention score matrix
nodes.definition: When both target and source are sequences, the matrix of scores with one row per target word and one column per source word.

nodes.name: Query, key and value
nodes.definition: The three inputs of attention: queries are scored against keys, and the scores weight a sum of values: sum(score(query, key) * value).

nodes.name: Parameterized attention
nodes.definition: Attention with learned Dense projections of the query, key and value inputs and of the output.

nodes.name: Scaling by 1/√d
nodes.definition: Dividing attention scores by the square root of the key/query vector size before the softmax.

nodes.name: Multi-head attention
nodes.definition: Several attention operations (heads) run in parallel on the same inputs, each with its own learned projections. Their outputs are concatenated and linearly projected.

nodes.name: Concatenation + output projection
nodes.definition: Stacking head outputs along the feature axis and mixing them with a final Dense layer.

nodes.name: Self-attention
nodes.definition: Attention in which the queries, keys and values all come from the same sequence, so each token attends to every token of its own sequence (including itself).

nodes.name: Why depth needs nonlinearity
nodes.definition: A stack of purely linear layers is equivalent to a single linear layer, so nonlinear activations are needed for depth to add expressive power.

nodes.name: Contextual representation
nodes.definition: A token vector that depends on the other tokens of the sequence, not only on the token itself.

nodes.name: Transformer encoder block
nodes.definition: A layer made of a self-attention sublayer and a position-wise feedforward sublayer, each followed by a residual addition and layer normalization.

nodes.name: Layer normalization
nodes.definition: Normalization that uses statistics computed within each sample (here, over the features of each token), independent of other samples in the batch.

nodes.name: Attention mask (padding mask)
nodes.definition: A Boolean tensor telling MultiHeadAttention which key positions each query may attend to.

nodes.name: Transformer decoder block
nodes.definition: A block like the encoder block but with two attention layers: self-attention over the target, then attention to the encoder output, followed by a feedforward network.

nodes.name: Cross-attention
nodes.definition: Attention in which the queries come from the decoder's target sequence and the keys and values come from the encoder's output sequence.

nodes.name: Causal attention mask
nodes.definition: A mask allowing each target position to attend only to itself and preceding positions.

nodes.name: Position-wise feedforward block
nodes.definition: Two Dense layers with a ReLU in between, applied to each token independently inside every Transformer block.

nodes.name: Source padding mask (`source != 0`)
nodes.definition: A boolean tensor marking real tokens (True) versus padding zeros (False) in the English input.

nodes.name: Order blindness of attention
nodes.definition: Attention computes interactions between pairs of tokens from their vectors alone, so it is insensitive to the order of the tokens: permuting the inputs permutes the outputs identically and leaves the scores unchanged.

nodes.name: Cyclic (sinusoidal) positional encoding
nodes.definition: The original Transformer's fixed position vectors with values in [-1, 1] varying cyclically with position.

nodes.name: Autoregressive (greedy) decoding
nodes.definition: Generating a sequence one token at a time. Each new token is chosen from the model's predicted distribution conditioned on the source and all previously generated tokens; greedy decoding always takes the most probable token.

nodes.name: Causal mask during generation
nodes.definition: The decoder's self-attention mask that prevents position $i$ from attending to positions $> i$.

nodes.name: Fixed-size learned positional embedding
nodes.definition: A learned `Embedding(sequence_length, dim)` table indexed by token position, added to token embeddings (Listing 15.17, p.475).

nodes.name: Data hunger and scalability of Transformers
nodes.definition: The tendency of Transformers to keep improving as data, depth and parameter count grow, while needing a lot of data to do well.
aliases: Data hunger and scalability of Transformers

nodes.name: BERT
nodes.definition: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, one of the first widely popular pretrained Transformers (Devlin et al.).

nodes.name: Masked language modeling
nodes.definition: A self-supervised pretraining objective: randomly replace about 15% of tokens with `[MASK]` and train the model to predict the original tokens from the rest of the sequence.

nodes.name: Tokenizer-model matching
nodes.definition: The requirement that inputs to a pretrained model be tokenized exactly as during pretraining.

nodes.name: Backbone
nodes.definition: A pretrained network that maps inputs to a latent representation and has no task-specific head.

nodes.name: KerasHub preset / from_preset()
nodes.definition: A named bundle of configuration, weights and tokenizer assets, loaded by the `from_preset()` class constructor.

nodes.name: Classification head
nodes.definition: Task-specific layers attached on top of a backbone to produce class predictions.

nodes.name: Where a Transformer's parameters live
nodes.definition: The breakdown of model size between embedding tables and the encoder stack.

nodes.name: Sequence packing with special tokens
nodes.definition: Formatting each tokenized input as `<s>` tokens `</s>` followed by `<pad>`s up to a fixed length, as during pretraining.

nodes.name: text_dataset_from_directory
nodes.definition: A Keras utility that turns a directory of class subfolders of .txt files into a batched tf.data.Dataset of (string, label) pairs.

nodes.name: Truncation to the maximum sequence length
nodes.definition: Cutting token sequences longer than `sequence_length` so they fit the model's fixed number of positions.
aliases: Truncation to the maximum sequence length

nodes.name: Pretraining data provenance
nodes.definition: Where the text used to pretrain a model comes from, and in what mixture.

nodes.name: Pooling a sequence into one vector
nodes.definition: Reducing a (batch, sequence_length, d) tensor of token representations to (batch, d) for sequence-level prediction.
aliases: Pooling a sequence into one vector

nodes.name: First-token pooling
nodes.definition: Using the encoder's output vector at position 0 (RoBERTa's `<s>` start token, BERT's `[CLS]`) as a fixed-size representation of the whole sequence.

nodes.name: Word2Vec
nodes.definition: A pretrained word embedding from Mikolov et al. (Google, 2013) whose training objective turns word co-occurrence into vector proximity.

nodes.name: Word arithmetic / magic vectors
nodes.definition: The emergent property that semantic relations are approximately constant vector offsets, so analogies can be solved by vector addition and subtraction.

nodes.name: Semantic continuity
nodes.definition: Moving a small distance in the embedding space changes the human-facing meaning only slightly.

nodes.name: Semantic interpolation
nodes.definition: The point between two embeddings represents an intermediate meaning between the two tokens.

nodes.name: Hebbian learning
nodes.definition: The neuroscience principle that connections between neurons that fire together are strengthened: 'neurons that fire together, wire together'.

nodes.name: Vector program
nodes.definition: A complex, highly nonlinear function stored in a Transformer that maps the latent embedding space onto itself; the deep-model generalization of Word2Vec's magic vectors.

nodes.name: Transformer as a continuous, interpolative database
nodes.definition: The view that a Transformer stores data and programs as a continuous vector space retrieved via input tokens, rather than as discrete entries.
aliases: Deep learning model as a static interpolative database
Transformer as a continuous, interpolative database

nodes.name: Hallucination
nodes.definition: Generated output that is fluent and plausible but inaccurate or meaningless.

nodes.name: Representation power
nodes.definition: How complex the functions a model can express are.

nodes.name: Masked language model
nodes.definition: A model that learns p(tokens|surrounding tokens) by predicting masked tokens from context on both sides.

nodes.name: Bidirectional attention
nodes.definition: Unmasked self-attention in which every position may attend to every other position.

nodes.name: Generative model
nodes.definition: A model that learns a distribution over data (text, images, audio) and can sample new examples from it.

nodes.name: Augmented intelligence
nodes.definition: The authors' framing of AI as a tool that augments human capabilities rather than replacing humans.

nodes.name: Large language model (LLM)
nodes.definition: A scaled-up language model, a Transformer trained to predict the next token on very large text corpora, as used in assistants like ChatGPT.

nodes.name: Mixture density network
nodes.definition: A network whose output layer gives the parameters of a mixture distribution over continuous targets.

nodes.name: GPT (Generative Pretrained Transformer)
nodes.definition: A Transformer language model pretrained to predict the next token on large text corpora, then fine-tuned or prompted for tasks.

nodes.name: Generative pretraining
nodes.definition: Self-supervised pretraining by predicting the next token, used to learn general-purpose representations.

nodes.name: Scaling
nodes.definition: Improving models by increasing parameters, data and compute with mostly unchanged methods.

nodes.name: Few-shot learning (in-context)
nodes.definition: Getting a model to do a new task from a handful of examples. In LLMs the examples are placed in the prompt.

nodes.name: Zero-shot prompting
nodes.definition: Specifying a task with a description and the input only, without examples.

nodes.name: Pretraining corpus
nodes.definition: The large body of unlabeled text a language model is pretrained on.

nodes.name: SentencePiece
nodes.definition: A fast C++ subword tokenization library with tokenize and detokenize operations.

nodes.name: End-of-text token and sequence packing
nodes.definition: Concatenating documents into one token stream separated by a special <|endoftext|> token and cutting the stream into fixed-length samples regardless of document boundaries.

nodes.name: Parallel input pipelines with tf.data
nodes.definition: Building the training input as a chain of tf.data transformations that run on CPU threads in parallel with training.

nodes.name: Input/label shift for language modeling
nodes.definition: Building training pairs from a chunk of $T+1$ tokens by using the first $T$ as inputs and the last $T$ as labels, so the label at position $t$ is the token at $t+1$.

nodes.name: Decoder-only Transformer (GPT)
nodes.definition: A Transformer with no encoder: a stack of causal self-attention + feedforward blocks over a single token sequence.

nodes.name: Windowing a token stream with rebatch()
nodes.definition: Using `Dataset.rebatch(n, drop_remainder=True)` on a dataset of variable-length 1-D token tensors to re-slice their concatenation into chunks of exactly `n` tokens.
aliases: Windowing a token stream with rebatch()

nodes.name: Weight tying (preview)
nodes.definition: Using the transpose of the input token-embedding matrix as the output projection to vocabulary logits.

nodes.name: Mixed precision
nodes.definition: Running most computations in a lower-precision float type (float16) while keeping variables in float32.

nodes.name: Learning-rate warmup
nodes.definition: Increasing the learning rate from (near) zero to its target value over the first steps of training.

nodes.name: Learning-rate schedule (Keras)
nodes.definition: A callable object that maps the training step to a learning rate and is passed to an optimizer in place of a constant.

nodes.name: Exploding gradients
nodes.definition: Gradients growing so large that parameter updates overshoot and the loss fails to converge.

nodes.name: steps_per_epoch / validation_steps
nodes.definition: fit() arguments that fix how many batches make up one epoch of training and of validation.

nodes.name: Logits and from_logits=True
nodes.definition: Unnormalized scores output by the model; passing from_logits=True tells the loss to apply the softmax itself.

nodes.name: Fixed input shapes and padding
nodes.definition: Keeping the input tensor shape constant across calls, padding when the real data is shorter.

nodes.name: Key/value caching
nodes.definition: Storing the key and value vectors of all previously processed positions at every attention layer of a causal Transformer, so that each generation step only computes the new token's query, key and value.

nodes.name: Compiled, shape-stable execution
nodes.definition: Running the model through Keras's compiled predict() with a fixed input shape so the backend optimizes and reuses one program.

nodes.name: Greedy search (greedy decoding)
nodes.definition: Choosing the single most likely token at every generation step.

nodes.name: Sampling strategy
nodes.definition: The rule that maps a model's predicted distribution to a chosen next token.

nodes.name: Sampling from a categorical distribution
nodes.definition: Drawing a token at random with probability equal to its softmax probability.

nodes.name: Softmax temperature
nodes.definition: A scalar T dividing the logits before softmax to control how peaked the sampling distribution is.

nodes.name: Top-K sampling
nodes.definition: Restricting sampling to the K most likely tokens.

nodes.name: functools.partial
nodes.definition: Creating a new function with some arguments of an existing one fixed.

nodes.name: Sampling temperature
nodes.definition: A scalar T dividing the logits before softmax to control how peaked the distribution is.

nodes.name: Beam search
nodes.definition: A decoding heuristic that keeps a fixed number of candidate sequences (beams) at each timestep.

nodes.name: Pretrained LLM
nodes.definition: A large language model already pretrained by a well-resourced organization, reused by others.

nodes.name: KerasHub task API (CausalLM)
nodes.definition: A high-level KerasHub model class that bundles a matching preprocessor and a pretrained architecture for a problem type.

nodes.name: Model terms of use
nodes.definition: License conditions you must accept to download and use model weights.

nodes.name: KerasHub CausalLM task
nodes.definition: A high-level KerasHub model that combines a text preprocessor (tokenizer plus packing/padding) with a Transformer backbone for next-token prediction, and provides fit(), predict() and generate().

nodes.name: Tied (reversible) token embedding
nodes.definition: Using the same matrix both to embed input token IDs into vectors and, transposed, to project the final hidden states back to vocabulary logits.

nodes.name: Instruction fine-tuning
nodes.definition: Further training of a pretrained LLM on instruction/response pairs, serialized into one marked-up sequence, using the standard next-token loss.

nodes.name: Prompt/response template
nodes.definition: A fixed text format with markers that wraps each instruction and response, used consistently in training and inference.

nodes.name: Loss masking with sample weights
nodes.definition: Using per-position weights to include only some positions (here response tokens) in the loss.

nodes.name: Training memory: weights, gradients, optimizer state
nodes.definition: Memory needed to train is weights + gradients + optimizer state + activations.
aliases: Training memory: weights, gradients, optimizer state

nodes.name: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
nodes.definition: A fine-tuning method that freezes pretrained weight matrices and learns an additive update factored as the product of two thin matrices.

nodes.name: Low-rank matrix
nodes.definition: A matrix whose rank (number of independent rows/columns) is much smaller than its dimensions; it factors as a product of thin matrices.

nodes.name: Freezing layers (trainable = False)
nodes.definition: Marking a layer or model as non-trainable so its weights receive no updates and need no optimizer state.

nodes.name: Training memory budget
nodes.definition: The accelerator memory needed for training: parameters + gradients + optimizer state + forward-pass activations.

nodes.name: Weighted metrics with sample weights
nodes.definition: Metrics passed via `weighted_metrics` in `compile()` are computed using the `sample_weight` supplied with each batch.

nodes.name: Refusal training
nodes.definition: Including instruction/response pairs whose target response is a refusal or 'I don't know'.

nodes.name: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
nodes.definition: Fine-tuning on hand-curated prompt/response pairs.

nodes.name: Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF)
nodes.definition: Training an LLM to maximize a reward model learned from human preference rankings, on top of SFT.
aliases: RLHF (as the template for CoT training)

nodes.name: Reward model
nodes.definition: A model, usually a smaller Transformer, mapping a prompt-response pair to a single float that proxies human preference.

nodes.name: Filter-and-fine-tune (rejection sampling)
nodes.definition: Generating candidates, keeping those above a reward threshold, and fine-tuning on them.

nodes.name: Instruction-tuned checkpoint
nodes.definition: A released model variant specialized for chat by SFT and preference tuning.

nodes.name: bfloat16 precision
nodes.definition: A 16-bit floating-point format with 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits and 7 mantissa bits; 2 bytes per value.

nodes.name: Chat / prompt template
nodes.definition: The fixed markup (here `<start_of_turn>user ... <end_of_turn>` and `<start_of_turn>model`) that delimits user and model turns in an instruction-tuned model's input.

nodes.name: Multimodal LLM
nodes.definition: A language model that processes inputs from more than one modality, here images together with text, in a single Transformer sequence.

nodes.name: Soft token (vs. hard token)
nodes.definition: A vector inserted directly into a Transformer's input sequence (e.g. by a vision encoder), as opposed to a hard token, which is a row of the embedding matrix selected by an integer ID.

nodes.name: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
nodes.definition: Using an LLM as the interface to information retrieved by a separate search or retrieval system, by inserting that information into the prompt.

nodes.name: Vector database
nodes.definition: A database that stores document text with an embedding vector as its key and returns the documents whose keys are closest to a query vector.

nodes.name: Chain-of-thought prompting
nodes.definition: Prompting an LLM, with worked examples or an instruction, to write out intermediate reasoning steps before the final answer.

nodes.name: Reasoning model / chain-of-thought fine-tuning
nodes.definition: An LLM trained, in an RLHF-like loop, to produce step-by-step solutions that lead to verifiably correct answers.

nodes.name: Random sampling (sampler="random")
nodes.definition: Choosing each next token by sampling from the model's full predicted probability distribution.

nodes.name: RL with verifiable rewards (rejection-sampling fine-tuning)
nodes.definition: Sample several responses, keep the ones an automatic checker marks correct, fine-tune on them, repeat.

nodes.name: Compute budget: parameters versus data
nodes.definition: With a fixed training budget measured in flops, you trade model size against the number of training tokens.

nodes.name: Scaling (compute, parameters, data)
nodes.definition: The empirical observation that LLM performance (next-token prediction) improves predictably as compute, model size and data grow.

nodes.name: Compute-optimal trade-off
nodes.definition: For a fixed pretraining budget, choosing model size and data size to get the best performance.

nodes.name: Deployment cost trade-off
nodes.definition: Choosing a smaller model than the best-performing one so it runs on cheaper hardware.

nodes.name: Pretraining data scarcity
nodes.definition: The supply of high-quality, public, human-written text is limited, constraining further scaling of dataset size.

nodes.name: Accelerator memory bottleneck
nodes.definition: The limit imposed by GPU/TPU memory on which models can be trained or served.

nodes.name: Image generation
nodes.definition: Creating new images by learning a latent visual space and sampling from it.

nodes.name: Generator / decoder
nodes.definition: The module that maps a latent point to an image.

nodes.name: Text-to-image model
nodes.definition: A model that maps a natural-language prompt into a latent space and decodes it to a matching image.

nodes.name: Latent-space interpolation
nodes.definition: Generating outputs from points between (or combining) the latent representations of training examples.

nodes.name: Autoencoder
nodes.definition: A network that encodes an input to a low-dimensional latent space and decodes it back, trained to reconstruct its input.

nodes.name: Variational autoencoder (VAE)
nodes.definition: An autoencoder that mixes deep learning with Bayesian inference, encoding inputs as distributions in latent space.

nodes.name: Generative adversarial network (GAN)
nodes.definition: A generator and discriminator trained against each other; one of the three common image-generation families.

nodes.name: Unconditioned image generation
nodes.definition: Sampling images from a latent space without text (or other) conditioning.

nodes.name: Concept vector
nodes.definition: A direction in latent space that corresponds to a meaningful attribute change.

nodes.name: Reparameterization (sampling) step
nodes.definition: Sampling a latent point as $z=\mu+\sigma\odot\epsilon$ with independent noise $\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Low-dimensional, sparse code
nodes.definition: The most common constraint on a classical autoencoder's code: few dimensions, mostly zeros.

nodes.name: Kullback-Leibler divergence
nodes.definition: A measure of how much one probability distribution differs from a reference distribution; used here as the VAE regularization loss toward a normal distribution centered on 0.

nodes.name: keras.random.SeedGenerator
nodes.definition: A stateful object that supplies fresh seeds to keras.random functions so that each call produces new random numbers in a backend-agnostic, traceable way.

nodes.name: Transposed convolution (Conv2DTranspose)
nodes.definition: A learnable upsampling layer that, with strides=2, doubles spatial resolution; it is the transpose of the linear map computed by a strided convolution.

nodes.name: Decoder / generator
nodes.definition: The network that maps latent points to images.

nodes.name: Overriding Model.compute_loss()
nodes.definition: Customizing training by redefining the method that computes the scalar loss from (x, y, y_pred), while keeping Keras's built-in train_step().

nodes.name: keras.metrics.Mean tracker
nodes.definition: A stateful metric that keeps a running average of the values passed to update_state().

nodes.name: Denoising autoencoder
nodes.definition: A model trained to map a corrupted input (noise, compression artifacts, low resolution) to its clean version.

nodes.name: Image super-resolution
nodes.definition: Producing a higher-resolution, cleaner image from a low-resolution, possibly noisy one.

nodes.name: Diffusion model
nodes.definition: A generative model that creates images by applying a learned denoiser repeatedly, starting from pure noise; in the book's words, 'a denoising autoencoder in a loop'.

nodes.name: Forward vs reverse diffusion
nodes.definition: Forward diffusion gradually adds noise to an image until it disperses into nothing; reverse diffusion gradually removes noise to produce an image.

nodes.name: Aspect-preserving crop
nodes.definition: Cropping the largest region with the target aspect ratio before resizing, to avoid distortion.

nodes.name: U-Net
nodes.definition: An encoder-decoder ConvNet that downsamples, processes at low resolution, and upsamples back, with skip connections between matching resolutions.

nodes.name: Concatenative skip connection
nodes.definition: Passing a feature map from an earlier layer directly to a later one and concatenating it along the channel axis.

nodes.name: Predicting the noise mask
nodes.definition: Training the denoiser to output the noise present in its input rather than the clean image.

nodes.name: Noise-rate conditioning by concatenation
nodes.definition: Feeding the scalar noise rate into a convolutional network by tiling it into a full-resolution channel and concatenating it with the image features.

nodes.name: Zero-initialized output layer
nodes.definition: Initializing the final layer's kernel to zeros so that the untrained model outputs zeros.

nodes.name: Diffusion time
nodes.definition: The index of the current step in the diffusion loop, a continuous value from 1 (pure noise) to 0 (pure signal).

nodes.name: Swish activation
nodes.definition: swish(x) = x · sigmoid(x), a smooth, non-monotonic alternative to ReLU.

nodes.name: Diffusion schedule (cosine)
nodes.definition: The mapping from diffusion time to (noise rate, signal rate). The book uses a cosine schedule: the rates are the sine and cosine of an angle that grows linearly with diffusion time.

nodes.name: Image normalization
nodes.definition: Standardizing images to zero mean and unit variance with a Normalization layer.

nodes.name: Reconstructing the image from predicted noise
nodes.definition: Recovering an estimate of the clean image by subtracting the predicted noise from the noisy image and rescaling by the signal rate.
aliases: Reconstructing the image from predicted noise

nodes.name: Reverse diffusion (generation loop)
nodes.definition: Generating images by starting from Gaussian noise and repeatedly denoising while decreasing the diffusion time from 1 toward 0.

nodes.name: Denormalization
nodes.definition: Inverting the input normalization: multiply by the standard deviation and add the mean.

nodes.name: Exponential moving average of weights (Polyak averaging)
nodes.definition: Maintaining a running exponential average of the model's weights during training and periodically using it as the model's weights.
aliases: Exponential moving average of weights (Polyak averaging)

nodes.name: AdamW
nodes.definition: The Adam optimizer with decoupled weight decay.

nodes.name: Text conditioning
nodes.definition: Supplying an embedding of a text caption to a generative model as an extra input, so the model learns p(image | text) instead of p(image).

nodes.name: Pretrained text encoder
nodes.definition: A Transformer encoder (the book suggests something like RoBERTa) that maps text to vectors in a continuous embedding space.

nodes.name: Stable Diffusion (KerasHub TextToImage)
nodes.definition: A pretrained open text-to-image diffusion model from Stability AI, available in KerasHub as a TextToImage task preset.

nodes.name: Negative prompt
nodes.definition: A second text input that steers the diffusion process away from images matching it.

nodes.name: Classifier-free guidance
nodes.definition: A sampling technique that extrapolates from an unconditional (or negative-prompt) noise prediction toward the conditional one by a guidance scale s.

nodes.name: Number of diffusion steps
nodes.definition: How many denoising iterations the sampler performs to go from pure noise to an image (num_steps).

nodes.name: Interpolating in a text embedding space
nodes.definition: Walking between two prompts' embeddings so that intermediate points, when denoised, produce images blending the two scenes.
aliases: Interpolating in a text embedding space

nodes.name: Model size vs memory
nodes.definition: Larger models produce better images but need proportionally more memory and compute.

nodes.name: Denoising in a compressed latent space
nodes.definition: Running the diffusion process on a smaller latent representation produced by an image autoencoder, then decoding the final latent into pixels.
aliases: Denoising in a compressed latent space

nodes.name: The four SD3 text-embedding tensors
nodes.definition: Positive and negative token sequences (1, 154, 4096) and positive and negative pooled vectors (1, 2048).

nodes.name: Spherical linear interpolation (slerp)
nodes.definition: Interpolation between two vectors along the great-circle arc connecting them, parameterized by t ∈ [0, 1].

nodes.name: Text-conditioned diffusion (text-to-image model)
nodes.definition: A diffusion model whose denoiser also receives text embeddings of a prompt, so the image it generates from noise follows the description.

nodes.name: Deep networks as interpolation machines
nodes.definition: The view that deep networks generalize by learning smooth mappings onto low-dimensional manifolds and then interpolating between the training examples on those manifolds.

nodes.name: Hyperparameter
nodes.definition: An architecture-level or training-configuration choice (number of layers, units, activation, use of BatchNormalization, dropout rate, ...) that is fixed before training and not learned by backpropagation.

nodes.name: Hyperparameter search space
nodes.definition: The set of hyperparameter choices declared in a model, each with a range or list of allowed values.

nodes.name: KerasTuner

nodes.name: Gradient-free optimization
nodes.definition: Optimization using only evaluations of the objective, without derivatives.

nodes.name: KerasTuner HyperModel
nodes.definition: A class (subclass of kt.HyperModel) that defines a search space through its build(hp) method and can carry configuration in its constructor.

nodes.name: KerasTuner hyperparameter types
nodes.definition: The kinds of hyperparameters you can declare: Int, Float, Boolean and Choice.

nodes.name: Tuner
nodes.definition: The object that runs the hyperparameter search loop: pick values, build the model, train it, record metrics.

nodes.name: Bayesian optimization
nodes.definition: A tuning strategy that predicts which new hyperparameter values are likely to perform best, given the outcomes of earlier trials.

nodes.name: kt.Objective (named metric with direction)
nodes.definition: An object telling the tuner which logged metric to optimize and whether to maximize or minimize it.

nodes.name: Retraining on training + validation data
nodes.definition: After all hyperparameters (including the epoch count) are fixed, train the final model from scratch on the union of the training and validation sets.

nodes.name: Validation-set overfitting
nodes.definition: When hyperparameters are selected using a validation set, they become fitted to that set, so validation performance overestimates generalization.

nodes.name: Model ensembling
nodes.definition: Pooling the predictions of a set of different models to produce better predictions.
nodes.chapter: 18 Best practices for the real world

nodes.name: Premade search spaces (HyperXception, HyperResNet)
nodes.definition: Ready-made KerasTuner hypermodels that are tunable versions of Keras Applications architectures.
